afc0831383b49f41: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry should assess the performance and readiness of 6-year-olds entering Year One during the voluntary intakes in 2027 and 2028, and publish its findings before making enrolment compulsory in 2029.

National Parents, Community and Private Sector Schools Engagement deputy chairman Zainol Abidin Mohamad said the 73,498 applications from families of six-year-olds for the 2027 school session reflected parents' interest and confidence in early enrolment.
"However, the number of applications alone cannot determine the success of an education policy.
"I propose that the voluntary intakes in 2027 and 2028 be used to conduct a comprehensive, evidence-based assessment of early entry into Year One," he said when contacted.

Zainol said the ministry should monitor pupils' academic progress, emotional wellbeing, social skills and stress levels, while gathering feedback from teachers and parents in urban, rural and remote areas.
"The findings should be shared openly with the public before enrolment becomes compulsory in 2029," he said.

He urged the ministry to consider allowing flexibility for children who were not ready for Year One at six, as their cognitive, emotional, social and physical development could vary even among those of the same age.
Zainol said he had yet to see a comprehensive pilot study report in the public domain demonstrating that six-year-olds were ready for compulsory entry into Year One.
He said the association supported the proposal in principle but called for Year One teachers to receive training in child development, helping pupils manage their emotions and teaching through play.
He also called for more teachers and pupil management assistants where needed, manageable class sizes and dedicated support for pupils with special educational needs.
"We need to look beyond how early a child starts school and judge success by how well the education system develops that child's potential," he said.
Yesterday, it was reported that the Education Ministry plans to make Year One enrolment compulsory for six-year-olds from 2029, following voluntary early-entry arrangements in 2027 and 2028.

Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said the three-year transition period would allow the ministry to ensure that preparations involving the curriculum, teacher training, infrastructure and classrooms were carried out continuously before the policy became mandatory.

9c0ac2de81277c4d: SHAH ALAM, Nov 25 — The restructuring of Selangor’s prayer time zones from three to nine, effective Jan 1, 2027, aims to ensure the smooth observance of religious obligations among Muslims in the state, said Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir.

He said the move was aimed at improving the accuracy of prayer time calculations by taking into account the geographical locations of the nine districts involved, namely Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat and Sepang.

Anhar said that under the existing three-zone system, Zone 1 covers five districts, while Zones 2 and 3 each cover two, but the new arrangement will provide each district with its own prayer timetable.

“This will significantly reduce the gap between actual and scheduled prayer times in the easternmost and westernmost areas. Residents in the eastern areas will no longer have to wait an additional four to six minutes, as they do under the existing system,” he told reporters at a briefing on Selangor’s prayer time zone restructuring here today.

Anhar said the need to revise prayer time arrangements arose partly from complaints and reviews that revealed inconsistencies in the timing of the call to prayer during Ramadan, disrupting Muslims’ observance of fasting.
“Several factors led to this decision. Firstly, we received numerous reports of the Maghrib call to prayer being sounded two to four minutes earlier than the actual prayer time during Ramadan.

“Our data shows that this happens every year. Upon verification, we found that some calls to prayer were sounded after the prescribed time, which did not invalidate the fast, while others were sounded before the actual prayer time at the respective locations,” the Selangor mufti said.

Anhar also assured Muslims that there was no cause for concern over the restructuring and advised them to check the prayer times for their respective districts on the Selangor State Mufti Department’s official website from Jan 1 next year.

He added that his office would step up efforts to explain the revised prayer time arrangements to mosque communities throughout Selangor to ensure the proper observance of religious obligations among Muslims in the state.
The prayer timetables for all nine districts, covering January to December next year, are now available for viewing and download on the Selangor State Mufti Department’s website, he said.

“Insya-Allah, discussions are under way to ensure that the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia’s (JAKIM) Iman mobile application displays Selangor’s prayer times by district rather than by zone,” he said. — Bernama
587aef35b0417fc7: BEIJING, Nov 25 — Chen Jining, the top Chinese Communist Party leader in Shanghai, is under investigation for “serious violations of discipline and law”, state media reported yesterday, using a common euphemism for corruption.

The probe against Politburo member Chen comes less than a month after the ruling party promised tighter discipline, and signals that President Xi Jinping’s sweeping 14-year anti-corruption campaign is still expanding.

Xi has purged dozens of top officials and overseen a clear-out of the military’s top brass in recent months as he prepares for a key party congress next year, where the 73-year-old president will oversee a leadership reshuffle and almost certainly secure a fourth term as party leader.
Chen is the latest top official to be probed by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the party’s anti-corruption body, state broadcaster CCTV said, without providing further details.
Corruption charges typically follow such investigations in China, suggesting Chen’s political career is effectively over.
The 62-year-old is the fourth member of the Politburo — an elite Communist Party decision-making body currently with 21 members — to face investigation during its current term, which began in 2022.
Chen’s removal “proves one thing: that no one is safe in today’s Chinese politics”, said Wen-Ti Sung of the Australian National University
“Xi said at the fifth plenum that anti-corruption is ‘always on the road’. Chen just became exhibit A,” Sung told AFP.
The fifth plenum of the party’s Central Committee, led by Xi, was held in late October and adopted a decision on reducing corruption, state news agency Xinhua said at the time.
Headed for the top

Jonathan Czin, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, said that “it’s really remarkable to dismiss a fourth Politburo member. Even after the 1989 Tiananmen crackdown, the Party only dismissed two Politburo members.”
“Chen’s case is especially striking because he is still young enough to serve another term”, he added.
Chen has been in post in Shanghai, one of the country’s most prosperous cities and a commercial and financial hub, since 2022.
He was seen as a candidate for eventual elevation to the party’s top leadership.
The last Shanghai party chief to be investigated for discipline breaches was Chen Liangyu — no relation to Chen Jining — who was removed from office in 2006.
Chen Liangyu was replaced by Xi in 2007.
Before moving to Shanghai, Chen Jining served as mayor of Beijing, China’s capital, from 2017 to 2022.
He also had stints as minister of environmental protection and president of China’s elite Tsinghua University, where he studied environmental engineering as a student in the 1980s.
He met with a delegation from the Swiss pharmaceutical company Roche in Shanghai last Wednesday, according to local media.
Shanghai leaders have previously gone on to the Politburo Standing Committee, the party’s highest decision-making body.
China’s current premier, Li Qiang, was formerly Shanghai party chief, while his predecessor in the city, Han Zheng, is China’s vice president.
Xi’s anti-corruption campaign has snared thousands of officials, including top generals Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, and fellow Politburo member Ma Xingrui earlier this year. — AFP
e6302deaebbee430: PUTRAJAYA: A former medical centre chief executive officer who was awarded RM810,000 for unfair dismissal during the Movement Control Order (MCO) six years ago has had the sum reduced to RM360,000 by the Court of Appeal.
The court found that although Datuk Dr Karen Pamela Soh was unfairly dismissed, her own conduct had contributed to her employer's loss of confidence in her.

A three-member bench comprising Datuk Ismail Brahim, Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly made the ruling after allowing part of Quality Health Care Sdn Bhd's appeal against the Industrial Court's award to Soh.
Soh, who earned RM30,000 a month, had flown to Kota Kinabalu on the first day of the MCO and returned about six weeks later after two scheduled return flights were cancelled.
Based on the facts of the case, Soh flew to Kota Kinabalu on March 18, 2020, to attend a monthly meeting with clinics there and deliver personal protective equipment (PPE).
However, two days before her departure, she had informed the clinics that there would be no major meeting and that discussions would instead be conducted via teleconference.
Ong, who delivered the judgment, said the Industrial Court had failed to consider Soh's short period of employment and her own conduct when determining the amount of backwages to be awarded.
He said Soh had served the company, which operates a medical centre in Subang Jaya, for slightly more than four months before she was dismissed.
Ong said that despite the main purpose of the trip having fallen through, Soh proceeded with her travel plans without informing the company's chairman.
She also failed to promptly inform the chairman that she could not return after her flights were cancelled.
"A chief executive officer who leaves the workplace on the first day of a national emergency, without informing the chairman, invites the reaction that followed.
"The Industrial Court ought to have weighed these matters. It did not," he said in his written grounds of judgment published by the Judiciary Department yesterday.
The judge said Soh also did not book another flight for 17 days after being informed that her second scheduled return flight had been cancelled.
She only booked a return flight a day after the company issued her a show-cause letter on April 29, 2020, over alleged absence without leave.
Meanwhile, the medical centre's staff had to manage without her, with another doctor stepping in to assist with its daily administration.
Soh returned on May 1 but was informed by the company five days later that her employment contract had expired and would not be extended.
On the quantum of the award, Ong said employees who were unfairly dismissed were not automatically entitled to the maximum 24 months' backwages.
He said backwages were meant to compensate employees for loss of earnings and not to penalise employers.
The court upheld the finding that Soh was dismissed without just cause or excuse but reduced her backwages from RM720,000 to RM360,000, equivalent to 12 months' salary.
It also quashed the RM90,000 award in salary in lieu of notice and the order for five per cent annual interest.
The company was represented by lawyers Datuk Roger Chin and Ariah Wani Karim, while Soh appeared in person.

afccdcb010158c67: If courts were fast and fair, nobody would need a viral post to go home
Originally published on Global Voices
Court of Appeal building in Lagos, Nigeria. Image by King ChristLike via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).

This post by Fatima Zahra Yahaya is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

In February 2025, a letter from a jailed man named Thomas Jonathan Biodun reached the public after some Nigerian Twitter influencers visited his prison to play a friendly football match with the inmates. Biodun was in jail over a debt of NGN 1,137,000 (USD 758). In the letter, he said he had asked for help online before, but someone had called him a scammer.

One of the influencers shared the letter on social media. Another influencer, Sir Dickson, who goes by the handle Wizarab10 on X, pushed it further, garnering over 2.5 million views in one post. In his post, Sir Dickson said, “Nobody should be in prison over a debt. It is not a criminal offense. I have spoken to @egi_nupe [another X influencer and lawyer], and we will be taking it up. Imagine rotting in prison because you’re poor.” A public donation campaign followed, and within weeks, it had raised enough money to clear the debt.
Punch Newspapers reported that Biodun walked out of Apapa Kirikiri Correctional Center and thanked everyone who helped.
Biodun’s story has a happy ending. But it raises a hard question: Should a person’s freedom depend on the benevolence of internet strangers and how many people share a post?
The problem behind this story

In February 2026, the Nigerian Correctional Service said that most people in its custody were still waiting for trial. Many of them have not been found guilty of any crime but remain in pre-trial detention. While some of them cannot pay bail, others cannot pay court fines. In Nigeria, the crime of being poor can land you in a jail cell.

Waiting is not a small thing. While a case drags on, a person may lose their job, business, or place to live. A family can lose its breadwinner, which can derail a whole family — or even a whole community’s livelihoods.
When the internet steps in
Jonathan Biodun is not the only person who turned to the internet to seek support for injustice.

Quadri Alabi, 17, went viral in 2023 when he stood in front of former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi’s campaign convoy. He spent months in Kirikiri Prison over a robbery charge that his lawyer, Inibehe Effiong, called baseless. Effiong also said the police recorded him under the wrong age, meaning he was charged and sentenced as an adult. On April 17, 2025, he was freed. The same day, Effiong asked the public on X to help his family move to a safer home, because they were still getting threats. The International Center for Investigative Reporting (ICIR) reported that more than NGN 3 million (over USD 21,965) was raised within two hours.

Emeka Nzeruike was arrested in 2015, when he was only 12 years old, over an alleged theft. He spent 10 years in prison waiting for trial. In July 2025, a lawyer named Alexander Nzeadi, who posts on X as @_youfoundalex, took up his case, and Emeka walked out of court.

The lawyer wrote that Emeka had been alone, afraid, and forgotten, with no trial and no lawyer. He then asked Nigerians to help Emeka heal, learn a skill, and start his life again now that he was finally free. The post was seen millions of times.
The other side of the story

Look closely at these cases. Biodun, Alabi, and Nzeruike were helped because their stories reached the right people. A letter found the right hands. A lawyer or a kind stranger posted at the right time.
Biodun said he was first called a scammer. That shows how difficult it can be to be believed online.
But what about the person nobody posts about? Not every inmate has a famous friend, a lawyer, or a loud voice to advocate on their behalf. For them, it can feel like no one is watching.
This is the worry. If help comes only to the stories that go viral, then luck decides who goes home. A sad story with a clear photo may win hearts, while a quiet case may be missed.
Raising money to pay for inmates’ legal fees or fines is not new, and it is not only done online.

In 2023, The Conclave reported that public-spirited people and a group called Prisoners Rehabilitation and Welfare Action (PRAWA), a non-governmental organization (NGO), paid fines to free 37 inmates from Kuje and Suleja prisons. The Interior Minister at the time had urged Nigerians to pay the fines of some prisoners to ease crowding in prisons.
Kindness is good. But justice should not depend on luck or others’ generosity.
A hope for smart leaders

I do not believe we should stop being kind. I believe we should fix the courts, so that kindness is not the only hope a poor person has. If courts were fast and fair, nobody would need a viral post to go home.
Social media is already doing one useful thing. It shows us real faces and real stories where the system is failing. Smart leaders, lawyers, and judges can listen, and they can fix it.
Until then, every shared post is a sign that Nigerians care. It is also a sign that the courts must do better. Everyone in Nigeria deserves a fair day in court.
Written by Guest Contributor

2b379f38c5d33ce7: KUCHING, Nov 25 — Sarawak DAP will contest the 13th Sarawak election despite its Pakatan Harapan ally PKR deciding to sit out the polls.

Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen said the party had the autonomy to decide what was best for Sarawak and remained committed to providing a stronger opposition to keep the ruling Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) in check.
He said PKR’s withdrawal made it even more important for DAP to remain in the electoral contest to ensure effective checks and balances in the State Legislative Assembly (DUN).
“Elections must not be seen as a destabilising force in any democratic society, but rather to reinforce the notion of check and balance (sic),” he said in a video message posted on Facebook.

For this coming election, DAP has finalised a 12-seat line-up, comprising Kota Sentosa, Batu Lintang, Padungan, Pending, Batu Kitang, Batu Kawa, Opar, Tanjong Batu, Pujut, Bukit Assek, Pelawan, and Meradong.

Among its candidates are Chong, who is returning to Kota Sentosa after representing the constituency from 2006 to 2021, Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Yuen in Batu Lintang, and incumbent Pending assemblywoman Violet Yong Wui Wui.
“We should not allow GPS to have absolute control of Sarawak’s DUN with zero opposition,” he said.

Chong alleged that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had given in to pressure from GPS to have PKR withdraw from the state election in exchange for the coalition’s continued support for the federal government.
He said GPS should use its political influence to expedite matters that would directly benefit ordinary Sarawakians.
With PKR’s withdrawal, Chong described DAP as the only opposition party in Sarawak with a long-standing record of remaining outside the ruling coalition.

He acknowledged the presence of other local opposition parties but questioned their ability to remain in opposition, citing past instances of elected representatives joining the ruling coalition after winning their seats.

He referred to former elected representatives from the Sarawak National Party and Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak, who joined the then Sarawak Barisan Nasional, as well as former Parti Sarawak Bersatu representatives who had subsequently joined GPS.
In the previous 2021 state election, DAP contested 26 of the 82 seats but won only Padungan through Chong and Pending through Yong.
This was a significant decline from its performance in the 2016 election, when DAP won seven of the 31 seats contested.
Besides PKR, Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional have also said they will not be contesting in the Sarawak polls. — The Borneo Post
*Editor’s note: DUN stands for Dewan Undangan Negeri (State Legislative Assembly).
272d0de9a1e0b48b: JOHOR BARU: Nine foreigner-managed business premises in the city centre had additional signboards removed, while two others were ordered to cease operations following enforcement action over licensing violations.
The Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) operation yesterday was conducted by its Licensing and Enforcement Departments along Jalan Wong Ah Fook, including near Komtar.
The premises were found displaying signboards featuring foreign languages and promoting food products imported from Nepal without the required licences.

State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the enforcement action was part of efforts to curb licensing abuses and ensure businesses complied with local authority regulations.
He said all 16 local authorities in Johor had never issued small trader licences to foreigners to operate at morning markets, night markets or farmers' markets.

"Licences issued under the names of Malaysians cannot be rented out, transferred or handed over to others without approval. Any misuse can result in enforcement action, including licence revocation," he said.
Jafni said although the premises had valid business licences until December this year, the licences did not exempt them from complying with advertising and other licensing requirements.
He said the two premises ordered to cease operations were found to have committed licensing violations.
He added that premises found flouting regulations could face further action, including suspension or non-renewal of their business licences.

7ce9caf43c66f847: TANGERANG, Nov 25 — Malaysia has proposed that senior Asean officials responsible for disaster management meet more often to improve coordination and speed up aid to member states hit by natural disasters.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the proposal took into account the long interval before the next ministerial meeting, scheduled for October next year in Laos.
“We would like senior officials to meet more often, if possible, so that we can coordinate our efforts and get aid quickly to countries hit by natural disasters,” he told Bernama here today.

Ahmad Zahid was met after attending the 14th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Management (AMMDM), the 15th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Asean Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER) and related meetings hosted by Indonesia.

Ahmad Zahid, who chairs the Central Disaster Management Committee, is on a five-day working visit to Indonesia and arrived in Jakarta on Tuesday after a series of meetings on rural development cooperation in Bali that began on Monday.
Ahmad Zahid said Asean member states had shown greater commitment to disaster management than in previous years, particularly in delivering aid on time and coordinating their responses.
“Aid has reached those affected on time, and we have seen Asean countries working together, whether or not they frequently experience disasters,” he said.

He said member states were also sharing their experience in managing disasters, particularly Indonesia, which hosts the Asean Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre) in Jakarta.
Timor-Leste, Asean’s newest member, had also shown its commitment by helping shape how member states coordinate and work together on disaster management, he said.
Ahmad Zahid said Laos, which will take over the AMMDM chairmanship next year, had begun putting previously agreed programmes into practice through a whole-of-government approach.
Ahmad Zahid said adopting new technology would help Asean prepare for the effects of climate change and global warming.
He said talks with Asean dialogue partners China, Japan and South Korea had offered fresh insights into early warning systems and the use of satellites to forecast rainfall and wind patterns.
“All Asean member states should adopt this new technology,” he said.
On haze, Ahmad Zahid said member states needed a common approach, although Malaysia had not raised the issue specifically at the meetings.
“We know we need to take new measures and use technology so that we can act before an incident occurs,” he said. — Bernama

c3d61a63468be891: SHAH ALAM, Nov 25 — Selangor will set prayer times by nine districts instead of three zones from January 1, ahead of Ramadan next year, to make worship timings more accurate for Muslims in the state, Harian Metro reported today.

Selangor Mufti Datuk Anhar Opir said the change was prompted partly by complaints and checks showing the Maghrib azan was inconsistent throughout Ramadan, which raised concerns about the validity of Muslims’ fasts.
“Residents in the east no longer need to wait four or even six minutes compared with the previous zone timing,” he was quoted as saying at a briefing on the change here.
He said the move bases prayer times on each district’s actual geographic position and narrows the gaps between areas.
The Muslim fasting month of Ramadan 2027 is expected to begin around February 8, subject to the moon sighting, which in Malaysia is confirmed by the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal.
The nine districts are Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat and Sepang.
Anhar said the old zones lumped districts together, with the first covering five districts and the second and third two each.
He said one reason for the change was complaints, and later checks, showing that the Maghrib azan was not consistent throughout Ramadan, raising concerns about the validity of Muslims’ fasts.
“There are many factors, but the first is that many Maghrib azan in early Ramadan came before the time, and our reports show it was four, three, even two minutes early,” he said.

Anhar said the data showed this happened every year, and that after verification, some calls came after the prayer time and so did not invalidate the fast, while others were indeed made before the time had set in at the location concerned.
He said Muslims need not worry about the change and should refer to the Selangor Mufti Department’s official website for their district’s timetable from January 1.
“We have already prepared the timetable for the nine districts from January to December next year, and it can be accessed and downloaded,” he said.

Anhar added that the department is in talks to include district-based Selangor prayer times in the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia’s Iman app, and will step up efforts to explain the change to every community in the state.
9df8326b2244749e: KUALA LUMPUR: A member of parliament has called for the revival of integrated task forces involving the armed forces and other enforcement agencies to curb the entry of undocumented migrants and address their presence in the country.

Datuk Seri Dr Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) said the government should adopt an approach similar to the National Task Force (NTF) and the compliance operations task force established during the Covid-19 pandemic.
He said he supported the armed forces chief's proposal on Sept 14 to revive integrated operations, such as the NTF, to tackle the issue of undocumented migrants.
"I fully agree and have raised several times in this House that addressing the issue of undocumented migrants requires the mobilisation of all relevant agencies, including the armed forces.

"According to him, the proposal has been submitted to the National Security Council. My question is, what is the latest development regarding this proposal?" he said during the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for the Defence Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat.

Radzi said the government should also consider reviving the compliance operations task force, which operated under Op Penawar during the pandemic, to address the presence of undocumented migrants already in the country.
He said while Op Benteng under the NTF focused on securing the country's borders against illegal entry, a similar approach to Op Penawar could be adopted for enforcement within the country.
"Both operations involved the mobilisation of all relevant agencies, including the armed forces.
"I urge the government to also involve military personnel in addressing the issue of undocumented migrants already in the country," he said.
ca171ab41a233d37: LONDON, Nov 25 — Household energy bills for millions of Britons are set to surge by more than a quarter from January, the sector regulator Ofgem announced today, as the Middle East war drives up wholesale gas prices.
The US-Iran conflict, which sharply reduced tanker traffic through the crucial Strait of Hormuz, has sent oil and gas prices soaring and raised concerns about a fresh spike in overall inflation.
Ofgem, which sets every quarter the price cap that suppliers can charge customers for electricity and gas, said the cap would increase 26 per cent in January.
That will add around £443 (RM2,385) to the typical annual bill, which will climb to about £2,166, Ofgem said.

“Conflict in the Middle East continues to drive energy costs higher, and we know this price increase will be a worry for many households as winter approaches,” said Ofgem’s director general for markets, Neil Kenward.

The increase will impact around 20 million households on standard contracts with variable tariffs. A further 10 million households on fixed-rate deals will be shielded from the rise as long as their contract remains in place.
The price hike means that millions of households will face higher payments even after the government hands out direct subsidies of £100 towards energy bills.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s government announced the one-off payment for 20 million households in its annual budget report in October, while also removing fixed fees on gas bills.
The government has also extended a temporary tax cut on household electricity prices.

Since the outbreak of the US-Iran war on 28 February, the price of European natural gas, measured by the Dutch TTF futures contract, has surged by around 190 per cent, rising to €92 per megawatt-hour from around €32.
Britain’s annual inflation rate reached a 12-month high in October at 3.6 per cent as the Middle East conflict drove up motor fuel costs.
The latest energy price cap increase is set to fuel inflation further next year, adding to cost-of-living pressures.
However, gas prices remain well below the levels seen at the height of the energy crisis in 2022 after Russia began its invasion of Ukraine.
The sharpest increase in the price cap came in October 2022, when it was raised by 80 per cent. — AFP

1593272f88fee842: JOHOR BARU: A police corporal was charged in the Sessions Court today with three counts of agreeing to accept RM3,000 in bribes in exchange for not taking action against a man over drug offences.
Hazizan Zainuddin, 37, pleaded not guilty to all three charges before Judge N Kanageswari and claimed trial.

According to the charges, Hazizan, who was attached to the Tangkak police headquarters' Narcotics Crime Investigation Department, allegedly agreed to accept cash payments of RM2,400, RM550 and RM50 without consideration.
The payments, totalling RM3,000, were transferred from a bank account belonging to a 38-year-old man into Hazizan's account, through a 47-year-old woman.

He was accused of agreeing to accept the money despite knowing that it was connected to his official duties, as an inducement not to take legal action against a 44-year-old man for offences under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
The offences were allegedly committed at a bank branch in Taman Orkid Baru, Labis, Segamat, on Oct 30, 2024.
The charges were framed under Section 165 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to two years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission prosecuting officer Alice Voon Mei Ling handled the prosecution, while Hazizan was represented by National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer K. Bharathi.

b6f7c4169c0c67b0: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysia has strongly condemned the Zionist Israel regime’s strikes in Gaza on November 23 that killed a staff member of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) and injured three others.

0ab022f6e2c2c1c0: SINGAPORE, Nov 25 — An Indonesian woman has been hauled to court for allegedly assaulting an 88-year-old woman in a Holland Close flat.
Kuriah Dulani Jaminah, 41, is accused of hurting the senior on multiple occasions between October 15 and 18 by shoving tissue into her mouth, slapping her, and force-feeding her.
Charges levied against Kuriah include six counts of voluntarily causing hurt and one count of using criminal force against a vulnerable person.
In the first incident on October 15, Kuriah allegedly used criminal force on the victim by shoving tissue into her mouth and against her face and hand, according to court documents seen by AsiaOne.

On the morning of October 16, Kuriah is said to have repeatedly grabbed and pulled the victim’s left hand and right arm and slapped her multiple times on her face, right hand and right arm, causing her pain.
That same afternoon, the woman allegedly pulled the victim’s head and hands, slapped her face, shoulders and hands, shoved tissue against her face and force-fed her.
Kuriah is accused of assaulting the senior on three occasions on October 17.
In one instance, she slapped the victim eight times and shoved a spoon into her mouth.
The next day, Kuriah allegedly slapped the victim 18 times and handled her roughly.
Her relationship with the victim was not disclosed in court documents.
A pre-trial conference has been scheduled for November 25.
If found guilty of using criminal force on a vulnerable person, Kuriah can be jailed for up to six months, or fined up to S$3,000 (RM9,500), or both.
For voluntarily causing hurt to a vulnerable person, she can be jailed for up to six years, fined up to S$10,000, or both. — AsiaOne
80817301357bf50e: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an afternoon thunderstorm advisory for parts of Perak, Sabah, Sarawak, and the Federal Territory of Labuan, warning of heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 5.00pm today.

The weather alert, released at 2.50pm, covers five central and northern districts in Perak: Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, and Batang Padang, alerting road users to potential travel disruptions ahead of the evening commute.

Across East Malaysia, the advisory blankets widespread southern, coastal, and interior localities in Sarawak, including Kuching, Serian, Sri Aman, and Limbang. The warning concurrently extends across Gedong and Simunjan in the Samarahan division, alongside Song and Kapit in the Kapit division.

In Sabah, stormy conditions are forecast across the Interior division, spanning Sipitang, Kuala Penyu, Beaufort, and Membakut, as well as the populous West Coast corridor covering Papar, Penampang, Putatan, Kota Kinabalu, Tuaran, and Kota Belud. The bulletin also includes Tawau, Kudat, and the Sandakan division (specifically Kinabatangan and Sandakan), alongside the offshore Federal Territory of Labuan.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings when satellite and radar indicators track rainfall intensity exceeding 20 millimetres per hour that is either imminent or expected to persist beyond an hour.

The department emphasised that these bulletins serve as short-term alerts with a maximum validity of six hours from the time of issuance, advising motorists and residents across the affected zones to exercise caution and take precautions against localised flash floods, sudden wind squalls, and falling trees.

ba5d4ba7c6817c72: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 25 — The Region 1 Marine Police Force (PPM) has crippled a transnational drug smuggling syndicate operating through sea routes following the seizure of over 103 kilogrammes (kg) of syabu (methamphetamine) worth RM5.36 million and the arrest of four men in operations in the waters off Tanjung Dawai and Sungai Petani, Kedah, recently.

Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (KDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the team conducting patrol at 9pm on November 14 detected a suspicious fibreglass boat about seven nautical miles from Pulau Sayak in the waters off Tanjung Dawai.
“When instructed to stop for inspection, the boat sped off and made several dangerous manoeuvres in a bid to evade capture.

“However, our team managed to intercept the boat after a 90-minute high-speed chase, and we arrested two Indonesian men who were on board,” he told a press conference at the Region One PPM Headquarters here today, which was also attended by Bukit Aman PPM commander SAC Shamsol Kassim.

Mohd Yusri said an inspection of the boat lead to the discovery of five white sacks containing 100 gold-coloured plastic packets labelled “VIP 666” filled with 103kg of syabu estimated to be worth RM5.36 million, which were concealed in a specially constructed compartment in the boat.
Following the arrests, he said police raided a house in Kampung Sungai Layar Hujung, Sungai Petani and detained two more men - a Malaysian and an Indonesian - on November 15.

“The 36-year-old Malaysian suspect, who is self-employed and runs a grocery shop, is believed to be the mastermind behind the drug trafficking syndicate, planning and coordinating the drug shipments, as well as offering RM12,000 for each trip to transport the drugs to Indonesia.

“Further investigations found that the two men arrested were believed to have made six trips to smuggle drugs from Malaysia to a neighbouring country via sea routes to avoid detection by the authorities,” he added.
Mohd Yusri said although the three Indonesian suspects had valid passports, they were believed to have entered the country through unofficial entry points to carry out the drug smuggling activities.
Police also seized the fibreglass boat and a Toyota Hilux four-wheel drive vehicle, while the seized drugs could feed the habit of 518,990 addicts.

He said further investigations are ongoing, including efforts to trace the syndicate’s distribution network, while all four suspects, aged between 31 and 36, are being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
The operation involved one officer and 18 personnel from the Region One PPM, with support from the Marine Intelligence Unit and patrol boats PSC 45, PSC 60 and PIB 01.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusri said Region One PPM recorded 151 drug-related cases from January to November this year, resulting in 180 arrests and seizures of illicit substances worth RM11.96 million.
In total, 2,375 cases were recorded, with 1,462 arrests and seizures, including forfeitures, valued at RM187.99 million. — Bernama

bde848edfd5f22ef: GEORGE TOWN: Muddy runoff from a collapsed slope overflowed onto a public road and entered three homes in Paya Terubong on Monday night.
The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) said its Engineering Department officers inspected Lebuh Rambai 13 at 9.30pm on Nov 23, following a public complaint received at 9pm.
The inspection found that muddy water had overflowed from public drains after heavy surface runoff, entering the rear of houses No. 3, 5 and 7.
In a statement today, MBPP said the project developer deployed workers for clean-up operations at the affected homes at 9.50pm that night, with clearing still ongoing this morning.

The developer's appointed consultant has submitted a landslide incident report for Taman Seri Rambai, alongside a proposed mitigation plan, compliance documents and site safety details, to the Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) for approval.
"The consultant will submit a long-term proposal and mitigation plan to MBPP on or before Nov 27 for due consideration," the council added.
As immediate measures, the developer has covered the collapsed slope with plastic sheets and repaired the earth drains and temporary retention ponds.

State authorities have held the developer and landowner of an adjacent condominium and road project responsible for the incident.

Emergency slope stabilisation works have since been approved for the Taman Seri Rambai landslide site.
64cc906732dacc53: KOTA BARU: Police chiefs in states bordering Thailand has been told to step up security following repeated attempts by drug syndicates to smuggle narcotics into Malaysia.

Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the move was part of ongoing efforts to strengthen border controls amid increased drug smuggling activities in the region.
He said several enforcement agencies, apart from the police, were also involved in monitoring and securing the country's entry points.

"Instructions have been given to all police chiefs in states bordering Thailand to strengthen security following the successful interception of numerous attempts to smuggle drugs into Malaysia by Thai authorities.
"Security measures at airports and along the country's borders had been further tightened following the incident in Jakarta," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after presenting a mock cheque to the family of the late Corporal Muhamad Alimi Kamarudin, who died in a road crash on Nov 18, at Kampung Padang Sepulih.

Hussein said the measures were also in line with the Home Ministry's short- and medium-term initiatives, including 17 measures outlined by the Home Minister to tighten security at the country's entry points.
He said drug trafficking networks had been operating for a long time, with narcotics originating from northern countries being trafficked into Malaysia.

He said Malaysia was also used as a transit point for drugs destined for Indonesia and the Philippines through Sabah and Sarawak, as well as other countries via air routes, including Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
"Enforcement agencies remain vigilant and are constantly monitoring the situation to combat these drug syndicates," he said.
Hussein said Malaysia maintained close cooperation with authorities in Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines, which were among the key countries linked to regional drug trafficking networks.
He said drug smuggling attempts could be intercepted before the narcotics entered Malaysia, detected within the country or, in some cases, reach Indonesia, where local authorities would take action.
"Information-sharing among the four countries — Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines — is crucial in helping enforcement agencies address the drug threat," he said.
Thai authorities recently foiled several attempts by drug smugglers to bring narcotics into Malaysia, with the latest involving the seizure of 50kg of syabu worth about RM2.5 million in Tak Bai.

52aeb4c0d575fd42: KUALA LUMPUR: YTL AI Labs, a subsidiary of YTL Power International Bhd has launched Cikgu ILMU, a free artificial intelligence (AI)-powered learning application designed to help Malaysian parents support their children's education.

Powered by ILMU, Malaysia's AI, the application is aligned with the national school curriculum, covering the Standard Primary School Curriculum and Standard Secondary School Curriculum from Year One to Form Five.

a243b3f65412f1e7: IPOH: The Perak government is drafting a dedicated policy to tackle mental health issues and suicidal behaviour among teenagers in the state.

He said the policy would adopt an integrated approach covering early screening, intervention and treatment, while strengthening the roles of teachers and parents.

Sivanesan said the state Health Department and state Education Department were finalising a special intervention module for teachers and students to improve mental health awareness and management in schools.

The health department is also expanding community support through the Community Mental Health Support Group (K-MindSet), which aims to raise awareness, reduce stigma and encourage early help-seeking, he said, adding that the initiative now covers all 12 districts.

Meanwhile, Perak has 45 psychiatrists, giving a ratio of one specialist to 49,517 residents compared with the national average of one to 69,860, though more are needed to meet the state's target of one to 40,000, he said.

"There are three child and adolescent psychiatrists in Perak, stationed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital and Taiping Hospital, respectively. However, Teluk Intan Hospital does not yet have a child and adolescent psychiatrist.

72a3568db7d26e39: KUCHING: Sarawak Parti Keadilan Rakyat's decision not to contest the 13th state election gives Gabungan Parti Sarawak an advantage while reshaping the state's political competition, political analysts said.
With local parties increasingly dominating Sarawak's electoral arena, the move shows how state and federal political interests are weighed when shaping election strategies, according to two analysts.

Academician Professor Datuk Dr Jayum Jawan, a Fellow of the Academy of Sciences Malaysia, said competition in Malay-Melanau majority constituencies is unlikely to seriously challenge Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu, particularly its Bumiputera wing.
"However, I foresee that in Dayak-majority areas, there will still be competition for Gabungan Parti Sarawak.

"As for Chinese-majority constituencies, although the Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP) appears effective under the leadership of Dr Sim Kui Hian (Deputy Premier of Sarawak), the DAP will still pose a challenge, particularly in urban areas," he said.
Yesterday, Sarawak PKR announced it would sit out the 13th Sarawak election out of respect for the spirit of cooperation and consensus with GPS in the unity government.

The decision was announced in a joint statement by Sarawak PKR advisor Datuk Seri Hafsah Harun, PKR central vice-president Roland Engan and Sarawak PKR State Leadership Council (MPN) chairman Mahmud Epah.

The stance is also aimed at preserving state and federal political stability and strengthening ties between both governments, particularly in fulfilling demands under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
Earlier, Amanah, Pas and Barisan Nasional (BN) also announced they would not contest the polls.

Universiti Malaya political analyst Datuk Prof Dr Awang Azman Awang Pawi said the development reinforces a trend centred on local parties, where Sarawak's interests, autonomy and aspirations increasingly drive political competition.
Beyond reducing challengers to GPS — which won 76 of 82 seats in the 2021 state election — he said the move paves the way for contests with fewer competing parties.

Based on candidate announcements so far, Awang Azman said the state constituencies of Gedong, Satok, Bukit Sari, Piasau and Senadin warrant close attention, while Tasik Biru could see a straight fight between GPS and Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS).
More significantly, he said, the shifting landscape could move competition away from party-ideological clashes towards evaluating policies, performance and development delivery.

"The competitive landscape this time is expected to shift the focus from party-ideological rivalry to competition based on policy, performance, and development. Key issues such as employment opportunities, public income, the cost of living, rural infrastructure, and the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 are likely to form the core of the debate.

"Yet, 'development politics' should not merely highlight government projects and allocations as it must also gauge the effectiveness of implementation and the equitable distribution of development outcomes among the people," he said.

Beyond the advantages for GPS, Awang Azman pointed to the implications of limited competition for voter choice and checks and balances within the State Legislative Assembly (DUN), underscoring the growing importance of audit institutions, a free press and civil society in ensuring accountability.
Nationally, PKR's decision should also be viewed through its strategic relationship with GPS, which holds 23 parliamentary seats won in the 15th general election (GE15), he said.
Awang Azman said the move reflects PKR prioritising national strategic interests over state-level competition.

While post-election dynamics remain subject to GPS's own deliberations, the decision could lay the groundwork for broader cooperation ahead of the 16th general election (GE16), particularly if another hung Parliament emerges, he said.

"However, the current understanding does not necessarily guarantee cooperation after GE16, as GPS retains full autonomy in determining its political direction, based on its mandate and the interests of Sarawak," he said.
On DAP being the sole Pakatan Harapan component contesting the polls, he said the differing approaches do not necessarily signal a coalition split, but rather distinct strategic priorities.

a3e1b2501c03ec2d: KOTA BARU: Malaysian police are awaiting intelligence from Indonesia on a RM229 million drug seizure in Sumatra to determine whether the syndicate has links to Malaysia.

Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said information from Indonesian authorities was needed to establish whether the syndicate had links to local networks.
"We have been in contact with the Indonesian authorities and are waiting for them to share information, particularly if the syndicate involved has links to Malaysia," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after visiting the family of the late Corporal Muhamad Alimi Kamarudin, who died in a road crash on Nov 18, at Kampung Padang Sepulih here today.
Hussein said intelligence-sharing between enforcement agencies was crucial to identifying and dismantling transnational drug trafficking networks.
He said Malaysian police would share intelligence with other countries whenever arrests or drug seizures involved foreign syndicates, with similar cooperation expected from their counterparts.
"Malaysia maintains good working relationships with enforcement agencies in Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Singapore to combat cross-border drug trafficking," he added.
He said every arrest and seizure would be followed by investigations to identify the syndicates involved, their members, those transporting the drugs and their intended destinations.
"This is important because we need to trace the entire network before we can dismantle the syndicate," he said.
Hussein said drug syndicates were constantly adapting their methods and exploiting different transportation channels to evade detection.
He said traffickers would use air or sea routes depending on available opportunities, with some concealing drugs in footwear.
He cited recent cases involving drugs hidden in shoes and trafficked to Japan and Indonesia.
"They are flexible and will always look for opportunities, especially when they believe enforcement authorities may have lowered their guard," he said.
Hussein said when security controls were tightened at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), syndicates would attempt to use other airports, including those in Penang and Ipoh.
"They are dynamic, so we must also stay ahead of them and take action one step further," he said.

It was reported yesterday that Indonesian police crippled an Indonesia-Malaysiadrug trafficking syndicate, seizing narcotics worth Rp1.01 trillion (RM229 million) in an operation targeting its network in Sumatra.
Indonesian news portal Kompas reported that five men were arrested, including a former motorcycle road racer believed to be a trusted associate of a fugitive drug syndicate mastermind.

a31be81c4522ca57: PHNOM PENH: Staunch allies China and Cambodia began joint military exercises on Wednesday, which Phnom Penh said were the largest yet, featuring nearly 3,000 personnel across three locations.

The eighth "Golden Dragon" exercises will focus on "joint counterterrorism and anti-piracy operations" as well as humanitarian relief, and run until mid-December, China's defence ministry said in a statement.
The opening ceremony was held at Ream Naval Base, located off Cambodia's southern coast in the Gulf of Thailand, where Chinese renovations have raised US concerns.
Washington says the base - which was originally built partly with US funds -- could give China a key strategic position near the disputed South China Sea, which Beijing claims almost in its entirety.
Cambodian leaders have repeatedly denied the base is for use by any single foreign power, and in January, a US warship made a port call there.
Cambodian prime minister Hun Manet announced in August that long-delayed joint military exercises with the United States would restart next year.
The two nations staged joint exercises for seven years before Phnom Penh scrapped them in early 2017, just months after holding its first Golden Dragon drills with China.
In remarks on Wednesday, Cambodian defence minister Tea Seiha said the exercises with China have "no intention of threatening or causing impact to any third country".
Instead, he said the drills were a contribution to the international community "to strengthen shared peace and humanitarian relief".
He said they covered operations on land, at sea and in the air, involving warships, drones, helicopters, armoured vehicles, artillery and command systems.
Royal Cambodian Armed Forces (RCAF) senior officer Pen Sokrethvithyea said they were bigger than last year's drills, which had been billed as the largest ever.
More than 2,900 personnel were involved, around 1,300 of them Chinese, he said.
Last year, the RCAF said nearly 900 Chinese military personnel and more than 1,300 Cambodian soldiers took part.
The Chinese defence ministry said this year's exercises were aimed at "strengthening political mutual trust and expanding military exchanges".
e07ab4f13b700289: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The government will consider naming a Kuala Lumpur street after the late National Laureate Datuk Seri A Samad Said and setting up a gallery to showcase his work, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.

639e18c060f28d0b: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia has benefited immensely as a trading nation, and this is reflected in its engagements with world leaders, particularly during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting held recently in Shenzhen, China.

7b7275fa54ebccfa: PUTRAJAYA: Ibu bapa boleh menggunakan aplikasi Cikgu ILMU yang baru dilancarkan untuk membantu anak memahami kerja sekolah menerusi penerangan langkah demi langkah berpandukan kurikulum sekolah di Malaysia, kata Pengarah Eksekutif YTL AI Labs, Yeoh Pei Lou.
Beliau berkata, aplikasi kecerdasan buatan (AI) itu dibangunkan bagi membantu ibu bapa membimbing pembelajaran anak tanpa mengira latar belakang pendidikan mereka.
“Ibu bapa hanya perlu mengambil gambar kerja sekolah anak dan Cikgu ILMU akan menerangkan konsep pembelajaran itu langkah demi langkah,” katanya pada majlis pelancaran aplikasi itu, hari ini.
Majlis disempurnakan Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim, serentak dengan pelancaran inisiatif pendidikan AI kebangsaan, 'AI Temu AI' di Pusat Konvensyen Antarabangsa Putrajaya (PICC).
Cikgu ILMU akan tersedia secara percuma di Apple App Store dan Google Play Store, bersama aplikasi pembantu AI yang boleh diajak berbual, ILMUchat.
Yeoh berkata, Cikgu ILMU menggunakan model AI tempatan, ILMU, dan dibangunkan berpandukan kurikulum kebangsaan bagi sekolah rendah dan menengah, meliputi Tahun 1 hingga Tingkatan 5.
“Kebanyakan aplikasi AI lain mungkin memberikan jawapan yang kelihatan meyakinkan, tetapi jawapan itu tidak semestinya menepati sukatan pelajaran sekolah kita,” katanya.

Sebagai contoh, Yeoh berkata seorang ibu yang kurang yakin dengan penguasaan bahasa Inggerisnya boleh mengambil gambar kerja sekolah bahasa Inggeris anaknya dan meminta Cikgu ILMU memberikan penerangan dalam bahasa Melayu.
Menurut syarikat itu, ibu bapa juga boleh mengemukakan soalan secara lisan dan mendengar penerangan dalam bahasa pilihan mereka, sama ada bahasa Melayu, Inggeris, Cina atau Tamil.

Selain membantu memahami kerja sekolah, YTL AI Labs berkata aplikasi itu boleh menghasilkan panduan ulang kaji yang mengandungi konsep penting, penerangan, rajah dan soalan latihan, yang boleh dicetak untuk pembelajaran tanpa sambungan internet.
Aplikasi itu turut menyediakan kad imbas interaktif dengan fungsi bacaan suara bagi membantu kanak-kanak mengulang kaji dan mengingati konsep penting dalam pelajaran.

Mengulas kebimbangan mengenai pendedahan kanak-kanak kepada AI, Yeoh berkata ibu bapa boleh menyediakan kuiz dan aktiviti pembelajaran untuk anak mereka menerusi ruangan khas dalam aplikasi itu tanpa perlu berinteraksi dengan chatbot AI.
“Mereka tidak boleh berbual dengan AI atau meminta jawapan daripadanya. Mereka perlu menjawab sendiri soalan diberikan,” katanya.
AI akan menyemak dan menganalisis jawapan mereka secara automatik tanpa berinteraksi secara langsung dengan kanak-kanak, sebelum menyediakan laporan prestasi sebaik sahaja kuiz selesai.
Yeoh berkata, laporan itu membantu ibu bapa mengenal pasti kekuatan anak masing-masing serta topik pelajaran yang memerlukan lebih perhatian.

Sementara itu, Anwar berkata penyediaan aplikasi AI seperti Cikgu ILMU secara percuma bertujuan menggalakkan penggunaan teknologi berkenaan lebih meluas, bermula dengan ibu bapa sebelum diperluas kepada anak-anak.
Dalam ucapannya, beliau menegaskan manusia mesti kekal mengawal penggunaan AI dan ibu bapa tidak seharusnya menyerahkan tanggungjawab mendidik anak sepenuhnya kepada sekolah.

Beliau berkata, teknologi canggih perlu dimanfaatkan untuk mendidik manusia, bukannya mesin, manakala pendidikan mesti terus menitikberatkan pembentukan sahsiah, penerapan nilai murni dan sikap menghormati orang lain.

61882cc557db0c21: NOVEMBER 25 — Every November, Americans ask one another, “What are you thankful for?” In Malaysia, the question arrives a few hours later and reads, “Did you apply the voucher?”
Somewhere over the Pacific, Thursday went missing.

We know all about Friday. We know when the sale goes live, which credit card earns extra points and precisely how much more we must spend to qualify for free delivery. The last of these is a branch of mathematics in which spending RM80 to save RM12 is considered a good result. Several people in my family hold advanced degrees.
But Thursday deserves a better press agent.

Consider what America has managed to pull off. A vast, argumentative republic has agreed to reserve the fourth Thursday in November for dinner. There are differences of opinion over practically everything, including whether a sweet potato improves upon the addition of marshmallows, a matter on which an international observer might reasonably request clarification. Still, people turn up. Someone cooks. Someone brings a pie. Someone is entrusted with the ice, having demonstrated at a previous gathering the limits of their usefulness in the kitchen.

And in the days before the meal comes the finest American contribution to the whole business. A colleague, a neighbour or a student a long way from home gets asked, quite casually, “Do you have plans for Thanksgiving?”

There is considerable grace in the wording. “Will you be alone?” requires a small confession. “Do you have plans?” allows a person to say, “Nothing yet,” at which point a chair can be found and the matter settled without anybody having to admit how much the invitation meant.

Malaysians understand this instinctively. At an open house, the person who says “I’ve already eaten” is generally understood to be making conversation. A plate appears anyway. The American who finds room for one more at Thanksgiving and the Malaysian auntie advancing with a second helping of rendang would get along beautifully. It is the guest seated between them one worries about.

An American diplomat once brought me Sierra Nevada Pale Ale for Deepavali. It was a particularly sound bit of diplomacy. It went rather well with the food, and neither side felt the need to issue a joint statement.

That is the America worth celebrating this week. A country reveals quite a bit about itself in the holidays it invents, and there is something immensely likeable about one whose central obligation is to think of somebody to thank. You can do it badly. You can mumble it, make it too long, embarrass your children. Even an awkward thank-you gives somebody at the table a piece of information they might otherwise have gone years without hearing.

So by all means enjoy Black Friday. If the headphones are half price and you actually need headphones, you have my blessing. But America has a rather good offer running the day before. Think of someone in Kuala Lumpur who might be eating alone and send six words.

He said fielding the 11 newcomers — a mix of professionals and youths from all component parties, accounting for about 14 per cent of the candidates — was part of efforts to rejuvenate the coalition and groom the next generation of state leaders.

"I would like to thank the incumbents who served GPS in the previous term and have stepped aside to make way for new faces. This is a step towards rejuvenating GPS," he said at a press conference after the announcement.

On the decision by unity government parties Barisan Nasional, Parti Keadilan Rakyat and Amanah to sit out the polls, Abang Johari expressed appreciation for their stance in preserving political stability in Sarawak.
Abang Johari, who is also Sarawak Premier and PBB president, confirmed he will defend the Gedong state seat for a second term, having previously held Satok for nine terms.
PBB forms GPS alongside Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and Progressive Democratic Party (PDP).
The Election Commission has set Saturday, Nov 28, for nominations, Dec 8 for early voting and Dec 12 for polling.
In the 2021 state election, GPS won 76 of the 82 seats, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) took four and DAP two.
52c6cfc0b5ccfd2f: PUTRAJAYA: Parents can use the newly launched Cikgu ILMU tool to break down their children’s schoolwork into step-by-step explanations based on Malaysia’s school curriculum, says YTL AI Labs executive director Yeoh Pei Lou.
She said the artificial intelligence (AI) tool was developed to help parents support their children’s learning regardless of their educational background.
"Parents only need to take a picture of the homework, and Cikgu ILMU will explain the learning concepts step by step," she said at its launch here today.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim officiated the launch at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre, which was held alongside the introduction of the national AI education initiative, "AI Temu AI".
Cikgu ILMU will be available for free on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store, alongside YTL’s conversational AI assistant, ILMUchat.
Yeoh said Cikgu ILMU was powered by the Malaysian AI model ILMU and designed around the national primary and secondary school curricula, covering Year 1 to Form 5.
"Most other AI tools may provide answers that appear convincing, but these answers may not necessarily align with our school syllabus," she said.
For example, Yeoh said a mother who was not confident in English could photograph her child’s English homework and ask Cikgu ILMU to explain it in Malay.
Parents can also speak to the tool and listen to explanations in their preferred language. The tool supports Malay, English, Chinese and Tamil, according to the company.
Beyond homework help, Cikgu ILMU can generate study guides containing key concepts, explanations, diagrams and practice questions, which can be printed for offline learning.
It also offers interactive flashcards with read-aloud audio to help children revise and remember key concepts.

Addressing concerns about young children’s exposure to AI, Yeoh said parents could generate quizzes and learning activities for their children to complete through a separate interface without interacting with a chatbot.
"They cannot chat with the AI or ask it for the answers; they have to answer the questions themselves," she said.
The AI checks and analyses their answers in the background, producing a performance report once the quiz is completed.
Yeoh said the report would help parents identify their children’s strengths and topics that require more attention.
Meanwhile, Anwar said making AI applications such as Cikgu ILMU available for free was intended to encourage wider adoption of the technology, beginning with parents and extending to their children.
In his speech, he stressed that people must remain in control of AI and that parents should not leave their children’s education entirely to schools.
He said advanced technology should be used to educate human beings, not machines, with education continuing to nurture character, values and respect for others.
51eeafe205f1fdad: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will consider naming a street here after the late National Laureate Datuk Seri A Samad Said and setting up a gallery to showcase his work, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
Fahmi said veteran journalist Datuk A. Kadir Jasin proposed naming the street in recognition of Samad's contributions to literature and journalism.

"We will look at these proposals, God willing. For me, what matters most is that we appreciate his work and remember that he championed the rights of ordinary people," he said at Masjid Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq in Bangsar.
Fahmi said a gallery was also worth considering to honour Samad and introduce his writing to younger readers.
"His works are still popular, but we need to introduce them to younger generations, particularly Gen Z and Gen Alpha," he said.
He had also spoken to one of Samad's children about copyright and how the family could preserve his writing, Fahmi said.
The national laureate, fondly known as Pak Samad, died at 6.10pm yesterday after receiving treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital for diabetes and age-related illness.
Hundreds of mourners, including relatives, fellow artists and members of the public, attended funeral prayers at the mosque, led by imam Muhammad Abid Ayub.
Among those present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Kadir and singer-composer Datuk M. Nasir.
Samad was laid to rest at the Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery today.
1e43e138c61a0afc: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysians lost RM7.33 billion to online scams since 2023, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the Dewan Rakyat today, warning that cyber fraud cases continue to climb with women and private sector employees bearing the brunt.
Between January 2023 and October 2026, the authorities recorded 192,869 online scam cases, resulting in 75,266 arrests and 69,665 charges brought to court, the home minister revealed.

The police logged 56,802 cases involving RM1.56 billion in losses for the first 10 months of this year alone, leading to 20,842 arrests and charges filed against 18,369 individuals across 17,985 investigation papers.
“This data allows us to draw only one conclusion: the trend of this crime is rising,” Saifuddin told the Lower House during Question Time.
Women outnumber men at a ratio of six to four, while private sector employees make up the largest occupational group targeted by fraudsters, the minister added.
Syndicates rely heavily on mule bank accounts to operate, with the authorities detecting 254,546 such accounts between 2023 and October this year, with 137,699 prosecuted so far.
Students make up a significant portion of those allowing their bank accounts to be used as mules, a trend Saifuddin described as “alarming”.
“These syndicates simply cannot operate without mule accounts,” he said.

Authorities have categorised online fraud into six primary modus operandi: telecommunications scams, e-financial crimes, love scams, e-commerce fraud, non-existent loans, and non-existent investment schemes.
By volume, telecommunications fraud topped the list with 73,043 cases involving RM2.132 billion in losses, followed by e-commerce scams with 50,749 cases totalling RM509 million.
But fake investment schemes proved to be the most financially devastating, accounting for RM3.4 billion in losses across 27,863 cases, or nearly half of the total amount lost since 2023.
f5c28175b4c3c4fe: KUALA LUMPUR: Under-pressure men's singles shuttler Eogene Ewe gave himself a much-needed morale boost by clearing his opening hurdle at the Syed Modi International in Lucknow on Wednesday.

The 21-year-old has failed to reach the quarter-finals in six successive individual tournaments since making the semi-finals of the Macau Open in June, his best outing this year.

Another national shuttler in need of a change in fortunes, Wong Ling Ching, also enjoyed an encouraging start in the women's singles.
The world No. 48 outplayed India's world No. 72 Aakarshi Kashyap 21-11, 21-10 in 37 minutes, having needed 75 minutes to beat the same opponent at the Australian Open in June.

Ling Ching, 23, has not progressed beyond the second round in individual competitions since at least March and will be looking to put an end to that frustrating run against either India's seventh seed Devika Sihag or Tanya Hemanth.

Meanwhile, men's doubles qualifiers Lau Yi Sheng-Lee Yi Bo continued their fine start in Lucknow with a 21-17, 21-16 victory over India's Abhyuday Choudhary-Ayush Makhija to advance to the second round.

a32669e0f7852200: SINGAPORE: Singaporean actor Darren Lim does not believe in deliberately leaving his four children an inheritance, saying he would rather they learn to work hard and earn what they want for themselves.

The 54-year-old shared his views during the second episode of his wife Evelyn Tan's podcast, Fine Whine, where the couple discussed retirement, financial planning and what they hope to leave behind for their children.
"I don't believe in leaving things behind for our children. I don't believe in giving them an inheritance. I don't believe in buying a house for them, or buying a car for them," Lim said.
When Tan, 52, asked if it might be better to set aside something for them, Lim said doing so could make them complacent.
"No, then you make them lazy people. You want them to fight for themselves. You want them to fight for the things that they want, you know. I think that's more important," he said.

"I don't want to make my children lazy, and I think I should not deprive them of an opportunity to really work hard for themselves, and then every single cent that they earn will become sweet," he added.
Tan eventually agreed with his outlook, saying: "The fruit that you pick for yourself always tastes better, right? Rather than having it served to you on a plate."

The couple, who married in 2004, have four children — daughter Kristen, 21, and sons Jairus, 19, Way, 16, and Elliot, 12. Lim said they have explained to their children from a young age that they will eventually have to build their own lives and become independent.
"And you will have to go and do whatever you need to do for your life, for yourself. And you cannot depend on us anymore," he said, recalling their family conversations.
Tan also pointed out that working too hard to build wealth for their children could cost them valuable family time.
"You don't want to give them so much materially that you lose them emotionally," she said, adding that parents must also consider their own retirement and quality of life.
Lim clarified that their children would not be left entirely empty-handed, as any assets left over after the couple's retirement will be divided equally among the four.
They hope to support themselves in their later years without putting financial pressure on their children.
But they do expect their children to care for and support them when the time comes.

f920b9efe9a677ef: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will maintain the country’s dual 5G network policy, says communications minister Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the policy not only gave users the confidence to communicate securely using technology from their preferred providers, but also allowed one network to act as a backup for the other.

"If anything happens to one network, the second network can be activated," he told reporters after launching the Nexsec 2026 cybersecurity event at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre today.
Fahmi said he had asked both network operators to discuss how users could continue receiving services through an alternative network in the event of disruptions.
Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) uses Ericsson equipment, while U Mobile uses technology from Huawei and ZTE.

The future of the country’s dual 5G network policy came under scrutiny following planned changes to DNB’s ownership structure. The government is expected to cease being a major shareholder, while CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL Power are set to gain greater control.
This raised concerns among analysts over whether the networks’ technological diversity can be maintained, particularly if future procurement decisions lead to both adopting similar technologies.
On Nov 12, EuroCham Malaysia said clarity and consistency in the country’s 5G policy could boost foreign investor confidence in making long-term business decisions.

Its CEO, Kati Ferry, said Malaysia’s approach of using both Western and Chinese technologies gave the country a competitive advantage while allowing companies to choose networks that best suited their operational needs.
33cc8804988d9c69: KUALA LUMPUR: Online platforms and artificial intelligence (AI) are accelerating the path to extremism, with radicalisation increasingly driven by a combination of personal grievances, online influences and other factors rather than ideology alone.

International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) International Institute of Islamic Thought and Civilisation fellow Dr Ahmad El-Muhammady said the traditional recruitment model, which involved people meeting, engaging in discussions and eventually being recruited, had been overtaken by digital platforms.
"Global events now trigger an emotional and cognitive reaction that is instant and worldwide, unlike in the newspaper era. In today's context, you read it and immediately react to it.
"The world is also seeing 'convergence radicalisation', where it is no longer about ideology alone, but multiple factors coming together to fuel radicalisation.
"It is no longer a problem confined to certain places or countries. It will have a global impact," he said.

He was speaking ata a session titled "Confronting Lone-Actor Extremism: Strengthening Psychological Insight, Operational Preparedness and Regional Cooperation" at the Regional Seminar on De-Radicalisation and Preventing Violent Extremism (RSDPVE) 2026 today.

Ahmad said daily exposure to images of civilian suffering and perceived injustice could have a significant emotional impact, while video games and films could normalise violence and contribute to what he described as "imitative violence".
"Imitative violence is when acts of violence committed elsewhere are copied globally. This has happened in schools. For example, school shootings are something new.
"If you look at the perpetrators, who are they? They are schoolchildren. Why did this trend not happen before?
"When I spoke to several schoolchildren, they told me they had been exposed to games and films. This is where they learn and copy things," he said.
He added that children were also connected through online communities where they interacted and shared their experiences.

Meanwhile, Australian Department of Home Affairs Countering Violent Extremism Policy director Kate Ponting, who spoke at the same session, said Australia's threat environment was becoming more diverse, fragmented and difficult to categorise.
"Violence is being driven by personal grievances, harmful online influences and overlapping belief systems rather than a single, coherent ideology.
"This was evident in cases where people idolised Nazism while also keeping ISIS flags in their rooms, which appeared contradictory," she said.
She said some people were driven towards violence first before finding ideologies to justify their actions, while the online environment had deteriorated year on year.
However, Ponting said violent video games themselves were not necessarily the problem, pointing instead to features such as chat functions that enabled users to interact and form connections.
She added that artificial intelligence was also allowing potential perpetrators to plan attacks and troubleshoot problems.
"The online environment has existed for years, so what is new now?
"I would say platforms are doing much less to moderate content while introducing more features to encourage engagement.
"The entire online ecosystem has deteriorated year on year and is more diverse than ever," she said.
Ponting said online networks also facilitated self-harm, animal cruelty and child sexual exploitation, blurring the lines between extremism and other forms of crime.
She added that young people could be radicalised rapidly online and mobilised with little warning, making them difficult to identify through traditional counter-terrorism approaches.

"An Australian Federal Police study of 55 counter-terrorism investigations that led to trials found that all involved boys aged between 12 and 17 who had been radicalised online and held mixed or unclear beliefs," she said.
"Radicalised young people do not look the way we expect them to, and our programmes need to evolve to address this younger, more diverse and more digitally connected group," she said.
To address the threat, Ponting said Australia regularly engaged with technology companies to develop measures to prevent online radicalisation.
She said the country had trialled pop-up warnings on TikTok and Roblox to alert users searching for violent extremist content that such material was illegal and direct them to support services.
