2cebbbb427ce8760: KUALA LUMPUR: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil remembers National Laureate Datuk Seri A. Samad Said walking barefoot on scorching tarmac during a Bersih rally to champion the people's rights.
Fahmi said the late writer, fondly known as Pak Samad, had shown courage by taking to the streets, proving he was not merely an acclaimed literary figure but also a champion of humanitarian causes.
He recalled the incident after paying his last respects at Masjid Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq in Bangsar yesterday.
Also present were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.
Fahmi said the ministry would consider proposals from veteran journalists and writers to honour Pak Samad's contributions to the country's literary landscape.

He added that Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) would be asked to review its collection of the laureate's poems and other works for possible broadcast as a tribute and to introduce his writing to younger generations.
"Insya-Allah, I will also ask RTM to review some of his poems and works so that we can find a suitable time to have them read on air," he said.

Born in Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, Melaka, on April 9, 1935, A. Samad was named the country's fourth National Laureate in 1985. His acclaimed works include the novels Salina, Sungai Mengalir Lesu and Hujan Pagi.
He died at Kuala Lumpur Hospital at 6.10pm yesterday after receiving treatment for diabetes and age-related ailments. He was laid to rest at Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery today.
48a7272b906eb027: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd’s net profit rose 0.9 per cent to RM208.46 million in the second quarter (2Q) ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM206.56 million in the same period last year.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, the bank said the rise was driven by higher revenue and lower taxation, partially offset by higher operating expenses and allowance for expected credit losses.
Revenue jumped to RM648.50 million for the quarter under review against RM626.23 million previously.
The bank said net interest income increased by RM37.9 million, or 7.7 per cent, to RM532.9 million, driven by growth in loans, advances and financing.
Its net interest margin (NIM) stood at 2.19 per cent compared with 2.32 per cent a year ago.
Other operating income decreased by RM15.6 million, or 11.9 per cent, mainly due to lower treasury and investment income, and lower service charges and fee income.
“This was partially offset by higher wealth management income,” it said.

It added that total revenue increased by RM22.3 million, or 3.6 per cent, to RM648.5 million, while operating expenses rose by RM18.1 million, or 6.1 per cent, mainly due to higher administration and general expenses, establishment expenses, and personnel expenses.

The bank declared a first interim dividend of 11.88 sen per share on 1.73 billion ordinary shares amounting to approximately RM205.55 million for the financial year ending March 31, 2027, payable December 30, 2026.

For the six months ended September 30, 2026 (6M FY2027), Alliance Bank reported a higher net profit of RM456.78 million, up from RM405.26 million last year. Revenue rose to RM1.27 billion from RM1.24 billion a year ago.
“The group remains cautiously optimistic in its outlook for FY2027, supported by a strong capital position, resilient balance sheet and disciplined execution.

“The group is well positioned to navigate external uncertainties while continuing to invest in growth, strengthen customer relationships and deliver sustainable returns to shareholders,” it added. — Bernama
493609e2feae0769: ANKARA: Lima anggota Tentera Udara Turki maut apabila sebuah helikopter jenis AS-532 terhempas semasa penerbangan latihan di wilayah Eskisehir, tengah Turki pada Selasa, menurut penyiar NTV, lapor Xinhua.

Anggota bomba dari Perbandaran Metropolitan Eskisehir turut tiba di lokasi nahas bagi membantu operasi SAR, menurut laporan itu.
f80dd4950a1989f7: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — CIMB Group posted a lower net profit of RM1.87 billion in the third quarter of 2026 ended September 30, 2026 (3Q 2026), down from RM2.07 billion in the same quarter a year ago.
Revenue for the quarter under review fell to RM5.42 billion from RM5.94 billion previously, in line with lower net interest income (NII) amid an easing net interest margin (NIM).

“Operating income declined 8.8 per cent quarter-on-quarter to RM5.42 billion from RM5.94 billion in 3Q 2025 as NII was impacted by an easing NIM, while non-interest income (NOII) declined from weaker fees and trading income, offsetting the robust wealth and treasury client sales income,” it said in a filing to Bursa Malaysia today.
On outlook, the group maintained a cautious outlook on the macroeconomic and business environment for the remainder of the year.
“Geopolitical developments and oil price fluctuations continue to contribute to uncertainty in the operating environment,” CIMB said.
The group would also remain focused on driving regional trade and its wealth management franchise, optimising funding costs and maintaining a prudent approach to balance sheet growth.
The group has completed RM446 million of share buybacks between September and October 2026 and declared a special dividend of RM596 million to be paid by the end of FY2026.
“This brings total year-to-date 2026 dividends amounting to RM2.72 billion or 25.15 sen per share,” it said. — Bernama
6761542c5b25026d: JAKARTA: Sovereign wealth fund Danantara Indonesia recorded a consolidated net profit of 259.6 trillion rupiah (US$14.19 billion) in its first annual financial report for 2025 released on Wednesday, which has been much anticipated by analysts and investors.

Established in February 2025, Danantara has been used by President Prabowo Subianto to drive the development of Southeast Asia's largest economy and help reach his goal of boosting growth to eight per cent from around five per cent in recent years.

The 2025 figures came a day after Danantara's investment arm said it expected to miss its 2026 net profit target by a wide margin due to losses from investments in local equities, though it anticipated a rapid recovery in 2027.

Prabowo has rapidly expanded the scope of the fund, which originally managed and invested the dividends of over 1,000 state companies but has now been tasked with monitoring commodity exports and bankrolling projects like the US$100 billion Giant Sea Wall.

Fitch Ratings and other analysts have flagged concerns about the potential use of Danantara as the government's off-budget spending vehicle, raising contingent liability risks, as Prabowo's budget deficit climbs close to the mandatory limit of three per cent of GDP.
Danantara is different from most other sovereign wealth funds because it was formed from a consolidation of state companies, rather than through fiscal or commodity surpluses.

Danantara's return on equity stood at 8.7 per cent in 2025, its chief executive Rosan Roeslani said. Its revenues were 3,073 trillion rupiah, and its assets totalled 11,607 trillion rupiah by the end of the year.
The figures presented were annualised, based on its April to December financial report, which was audited by Indonesia's Supreme Audit Board.
Finalising its first financial report took a long time because of the sheer number of companies it manages, one of its managing directors Pahala Mansury said.
33f691270075a9f7: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysia must rapidly upgrade its national cybersecurity defences in lockstep with physical infrastructure investments to shield the country from emerging vulnerabilities posed by quantum computing and autonomous rogue agentic artificial intelligence, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.

Addressing the opening of the NEXSEC2026 cybersecurity conference at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC), Fahmi said that the government is prioritising quantum migration and post-quantum cryptography to prevent sensitive data traversing domestic telecommunications networks from being compromised.

“This is why I have tasked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) with convening research and development discussions on quantum migration and quantum-safe communications involving telecommunications companies and infrastructure providers.

“The shift towards quantum-safe communications is increasingly important to ensure data transmitted through telecommunications networks remains protected against interception, theft and hacking by cybercriminals,” he said.

Quantum migration involves upgrading legacy encryption protocols and security architecture to quantum-resistant algorithms capable of withstanding the unprecedented processing power of future quantum supercomputers.

For Malaysia, this transition requires retrofitting national telecommunication backbones and cloud routing systems to neutralize “harvest-now, decrypt-later” surveillance threats before quantum machines reach commercial maturity.
Fahmi warned that constructing world-class fibre and data centre infrastructure yields little value if sovereign data remains exposed to sophisticated digital intrusion.

However, he acknowledged that transitioning to quantum-safe communications entails substantial capital outlays, urging telecommunications operators and digital infrastructure concessionaires to strategically balance baseline capacity expansions with targeted cybersecurity expenditures.

The minister’s directive was delivered during NEXSEC2026, MCMC’s flagship cybersecurity symposium convened to assess sector readiness, accelerate advanced cyber engineering talent, and expand threat intelligence sharing among network operators, statutory agencies, and tertiary research institutions.
4cadb42cd21023df: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has filed two lawsuits against Google LLC, seeking a total of RM600 million in damages over its alleged failure to adequately address harmful content on YouTube.
In each suit, MCMC is seeking RM100 million in general damages, RM100 million in aggravated damages and RM100 million in exemplary damages.

"The damages sought are intended to remedy the substantial resources and manpower expended in addressing more than 50,000 pieces of harmful online content arising from Google's systemic failure, and to ensure a safe social media platform," it said in a statement today.
It said the damages were also intended to deter future non-compliance.
MCMC said the first suit concerned Google’s alleged failure to take adequate measures against thousands of pieces of harmful content, including material involving online gambling, scams and fraud.

The regulator said the suit was based on alleged negligence and breaches of statutory obligations and licence conditions. It said it submitted 74,703 reports to YouTube between Jan 1 and Oct 28 this year, of which 74,569, or 99.8%, concerned online gambling.
Of the gambling-related reports, YouTube responded to 32,781 or took them down within a day, while 4,950 received no response.
MCMC said 1,468 cases took more than 30 days to receive a response or have the content taken down, while 35 took more than 90 days.
"These figures demonstrate the scale of harmful content on the platform and the delays in addressing such content," it said.
The second suit concerns Google’s alleged failure to take statutory and proactive measures in relation to content reposted on YouTube by blogger Wan Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo.
MCMC said the content was subject to an interim injunction issued by the Kuala Lumpur High Court on June 19.

The regulator said social media platform providers subject to the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and the Online Safety Act 2025 must comply with their statutory obligations and licence conditions.
It said the lawsuits were part of efforts to protect the public, particularly children, from online harm.
4ab3b2cd6eaff33b: PUTRAJAYA: Perdana Menteri, Anwar Ibrahim mahu pemberian bantuan awal persekolahan (BAP) bagi sesi persekolahan 2027 dibuat di sekolah bagi menggalakkan ibu bapa hadir menemui guru, sekali gus dapat membincangkan perihal pendidikan anak.
Anwar yang juga menteri kewangan berkata, ibu bapa perlu ke sekolah anak untuk menerima bantuan itu, yang dinaikkan kepada RM200 tahun depan, berbanding RM150 sebelum ini bagi setiap murid.

“Sebab itulah saya beritahu kepada Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM) bahawa tahun depan, anak-anak akan dapat RM200. Tetapi, kita tidak serahkan wang itu ke rumah (bagi kes tertentu) kerana kita mahu ibu bapa datang sendiri ke sekolah berjumpa dengan guru-guru.”
Katanya ketika berucap pada majlis Peluncuran Prakarsa Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) Pendidikan Negara "AI Temu AI" di sini.
Beliau berkata, pihak sekolah disaran mengatur sesi pertemuan guru, murid dan ibu bapa bagi membolehkan guru berkongsi perkembangan serta tingkah laku murid di sekolah.

Anwar ketika membentangkan Belanjawan 2027 pada 9 Okt lalu mengumumkan BAP tahun depan dinaikkan daripada RM150 kepada RM200 bagi setiap murid, membabitkan 5.3 juta penerima dengan peruntukan keseluruhan RM1 bilion.

Dalam pada itu, Anwar mengingatkan ibu bapa tidak meletakkan sepenuhnya tanggungjawab mendidik murid kepada pihak sekolah, sebaliknya mereka perlu memainkan peranan bersama guru dalam membentuk sahsiah dan disiplin anak-anak.
Tegasnya, pendidikan bukan sekadar proses menimba ilmu, sebaliknya bagi membentuk manusia baik, berdisiplin dan mempunyai nilai akhlak yang memerlukan kerjasama rapat antara ibu bapa dengan guru.
Beliau turut mengingatkan murid supaya menghargai pengorbanan ibu bapa, termasuk menunjukkan kasih sayang dan menghormati mereka.

Anwar meminta KPM memastikan setiap murid diberi judul buku untuk dibaca sepanjang cuti persekolahan bulan depan dengan sekurang-kurangnya dua buku perlu habis dibaca bagi memastikan budaya membaca terus dapat dipupuk meskipun ketika bercuti.

5af12edb69a3cf9f: KUCHING, Nov 25 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) is fielding 11 new faces among the 82 candidates announced by its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg for the 13th Sarawak state election.

The revamped line-up, announced at Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) headquarters here, also features five women candidates, reflecting the coalition’s continued efforts to ensure female representation in the state’s political leadership.

The new faces are Wong Duk Ying (Padungan), Dayang Nurfizawati Abang Abdul Karim (Muara Tuang), Yussuf Chik (Simunjan), Awang Nashfarini Awang Sarbini (Beting Maro), Leonard Libau Anol (Simanggang), Nor-E-Fadzwie Salleh (Kabong), Alexander Donald (Ngemah), Kevin Lau Kor Jie (Bawang Assan), Cerisologo Sabut (Pelagus), Nur Fatin Syafawani Tahamat (Bekenu) and Datu Jack Liam (Batu Danau).

Several of the new candidates will be taking over from seasoned incumbents including Bawang Assan, where Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh is stepping aside after seven terms, as well as Simanggang and Bekenu, previously represented by Datuk Francis Harden Hollis and Datuk Rosey Yunus, who had served six and four terms respectively.
Abang Johari, who is caretaker premier, said the 11 new faces accounted for 14 per cent of the coalition’s total line-up.
“The average age of the new candidates is approximately between 40 and 50 years old,” he told a press conference at the PBB headquarters here.
He said the new line-up reflected GPS’ decision to give more opportunities to incoming leaders and broaden participation within its component parties.
“I would like to thank those who have served as GPS representatives in the previous term. I also thank those who have decided to step aside and give new faces an opportunity.
“This is part of our process of rejuvenating GPS and its respective component parties,” he said.
Abang Johari said the new GPS candidate line-up also sees an increase in women’s representation, with five female candidates being fielded compared to four in the previous state election.

They are Datuk Seri Fatimah Abdullah (Dalat), Datuk Sharifah Hasidah Sayeed Aman Ghazali (Samariang), Dayang Noorazah Awang Sohor (Lingga), as well as the two new faces, Nur Fatin Syafawani and Dayang Nurfizawati.
“We have also included more youths or young candidates which shows that we are recognising the capabilities of young people in the coming election.
“In fact, all the component parties have fielded young candidates. For example, our candidate contesting in Beting Maro is only 35 years old,” he said.

The candidate announcement also saw several significant changes in seat representation, particularly involving the Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), which will field 18 candidates, including incumbents See Chee How and Dr Johnichal Rayong Ngipa in Batu Lintang and Engkilili respectively.
Both constituencies are traditionally SUPP seats, although they were won by Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) candidates in the 2021 state election.

See won Batu Lintang under the PSB ticket in 2021 and subsequently served as an independent assemblyman after leaving the party in 2022, while Rayong won Engkilili under PSB before joining the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) in 2024 following PSB’s dissolution.
Rayong recently resigned from PDP, effective November 22, alongside Soon Koh, with both maintaining their support for GPS and Abang Johari’s leadership.
For Bawang Assan, GPS has fielded Lau under the SUPP ticket, while PDP president Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing will defend Dudong.
In terms of the overall seat distribution, PBB remains the largest component party with 47 candidates, followed by SUPP with 18, Parti Rakyat Sarawak with 11 and PDP with six.

The line-up maintains the same overall distribution as the original GPS seat allocation in the 2021 election, although the political circumstances surrounding several constituencies have since changed.

Abang Johari also expressed appreciation to parties which will not be contesting against GPS this state election, particularly its partners in the federal unity government, namely Barisan Nasional, Parti Amanah Negara and PKR.
“We want to maintain the political stability that Sarawak currently enjoys and leave it to the people to continue our efforts to develop Sarawak into a developed and prosperous region,” he said.

He said GPS wanted to maintain Sarawak’s political stability and leave it to the people to decide whether to continue the coalition’s efforts to develop the state into a developed and prosperous region.
On the health of the candidates, Abang Johari said all retained candidates had undergone medical examinations and were found to be healthy.
He also acknowledged that some incumbents had chosen to step aside voluntarily. — The Borneo Post

7ff0885441117eac: KUALA LUMPUR: Menteri Komunikasi Fahmi Fadzil mengarahkan Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) mengambil langkah bersama pemain industri telekomunikasi bagi melindungi sistem komunikasi negara daripada ancaman pengkomputeran kuantum.
Beliau berkata, Malaysia perlu bersedia beralih kepada sistem komunikasi yang mampu menghadapi risiko keselamatan seiring perkembangan teknologi itu, sebagai persediaan memasuki era pascakuantum.

Sehubungan itu, Fahmi mahu MCMC mengadakan perbincangan meja bulat mengenai penyelidikan dan pembangunan (R&D), disusuli tindakan bersama pemain industri bagi memastikan kesiapsiagaan infrastruktur maklumat negara.
Katanya, persediaan membabitkan pengendali rangkaian mudah alih, syarikat infrastruktur dan telekomunikasi itu memerlukan kos, sekali gus menuntut penelitian semula terhadap kaedah pengagihan sumber.

“Tiada gunanya mempunyai infrastruktur atau seni bina maklumat bertaraf dunia jika tidak disertai keselamatan siber bertaraf dunia,” katanya ketika berucap merasmikan NEXSEC2026 anjuran MCMC di Pusat Pameran dan Perdagangan Antarabangsa Malaysia (Mitec).

Fahmi berkata, keperluan menghadapi era migrasi kuantum semakin mendapat perhatian masyarakat antarabangsa, seperti dibincangkan pada persidangan Kesatuan Telekomunikasi Antarabangsa (ITU) di Doha baru-baru ini.

Katanya, cabaran keselamatan siber juga semakin kompleks apabila ancaman tidak lagi terhad kepada aktor negara dan bukan negara, malah turut membabitkan kecerdasan buatan (AI) agentik yang mampu bertindak di luar arahan asal.

“Agentik AI berupaya untuk keluar daripada kepompong ataupun daripada pusat latihan ataupun lingkungan latihannya untuk mengambil alih dan melakukan perkara-perkara yang bukan dalam arahan asal,” katanya.

Dalam pada itu, Fahmi berkata usaha MCMC bersama syarikat telekomunikasi membanteras penipuan dalam talian, termasuk menerusi langkah di peringkat rangkaian, membuahkan hasil, namun penjenayah terus mencari kaedah baharu.
MCMC dalam kenyataan memaklumkan, laporan Global Anti-Scam Alliance (Gasa) yang diterima Fahmi menganggarkan kerugian akibat penipuan di Malaysia mencecah RM19.7 bilion dalam tempoh setahun.

Pada majlis itu, MCMC turut memeterai memorandum persefahaman (MoU) dengan Agensi Keselamatan Siber Negara (Nacsa) bagi memperkukuh perkongsian maklumat ancaman siber, penyelarasan tindak balas serta pembangunan keupayaan kedua-dua agensi.

NEXSEC2026 yang berlangsung selama dua hari bermula hari ini menghimpunkan wakil kerajaan, agensi keselamatan, industri, institusi pengajian tinggi serta negara anggota Asean bagi memperkukuh kesiapsiagaan dan daya tahan siber negara.
65ab14ef181e309e: TUMPAT: The Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) pilot detained in a case involving a drug smuggling syndicate that used military assets was responsible for transporting drug supplies from the Klang Valley to Sabah, federal police said today.
Bukit Aman narcotics crime investigation department director Hussein Omar Khan said the individual was among the syndicate members assigned specific roles in its operations.
“He is one of the members. Apart from his role as the coordinator, he also served as a transporter, moving drug supplies from the Klang Valley to Sabah,” he told reporters here today.

Hussein said investigations had so far confirmed that the drugs were transported to Labuan and Tawau, but police did not rule out the possibility that the syndicate had also targeted other destinations.
He said 13 people had been detained so far to assist in investigations, comprising seven RMAF officers and personnel and six civilians.
Police had also identified several other people believed to be linked to the syndicate, with efforts underway to track them down and arrest them.

On the chronology of the investigation, Hussein said police first received information about the possible use of military assets in drug smuggling following a major drug seizure in January this year involving six containers at Port Klang that were bound for Teluk Sepanggar, Sabah.
He said police obtained more concrete information in July, before opening an investigation paper and continuing intelligence gathering and surveillance until the latest incident in Subang.

On Nov 19, police said they had uncovered a drug trafficking syndicate believed to have used RMAF air transport facilities to smuggle drugs into Sabah before distributing them to international markets, following the arrest of 11 people, including five RMAF officers.
Police arrested them during several raids conducted in collaboration with the RMAF in the Klang Valley and Labuan on Nov 17.

Defence minister Khaled Nordin said the arrests followed the discovery of drugs concealed in five suitcases and a box at the air movement building at the Subang air base. It was the first such incident detected through routine inspection.

Syndicates could target Sultan Ismail Petra Airport Hussein said drug smuggling syndicates could also target Sultan Ismail Petra Airport in Kota Bharu, citing attempts to use other airports since security was tightened at KLIA.
"When we tightened security at KLIA, there were attempts to use the airports in Penang and Ipoh. We believe these syndicates will target other airports, too," he said.
He called for tighter security at all airports nationwide, saying the attempts showed that syndicates would seize any opportunity to evade the heightened security at KLIA.

89ca6cde5308f10c: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 25 — Having parents collect the RM200 back-to-school aid in person gives them a chance to speak directly with teachers about their children’s behaviour and take a more active role in their education, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Anwar urged principals to use the aid collection sessions to give teachers an opportunity to raise concerns about pupils’ behaviour with their parents. “Parents also must be responsible. Issues of discipline, bullying, morals, are the responsibility of teachers in schools, but don’t leave it all to schools. “We want parents to know their children’s schools, meet the teachers, and teachers can give advice,” he said at the launch of a national initiative to use artificial intelligence (AI) in schools at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC).“And if they don’t come to school, Fadhlina, don’t give that money,” he quipped, addressing Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek. When tabling Budget 2027 on October 9, Anwar announced that the Bantuan Awal Persekolahan would rise from RM150 to RM200 per pupil and be distributed at schools. Anwar also urged students to show respect and appreciation for their teachers, who were making an effort to teach AI while learning to use it themselves. He said AI could help students learn things their parents might be unfamiliar with, and urged them to hug their parents and be patient with them as they adjusted to this new way of learning. Anwar said Malaysia would be left behind if Malaysians failed to master AI, likening the shift to the Industrial Revolution. He said AI, like computers and other tools, could be used for good or harmful purposes. “So students must master AI because it helps us, but remember that we are humans, we have religion, we have akhlak (character). “Therefore, it is not AI that masters us, we should master AI.” Anwar said schools would continue teaching reading and arithmetic through conventional methods while giving students early exposure to AI. “But the ministry, teachers should always remember that we use this advanced technology, AI, to educate humans, not educate machines ... Humans have character, religion, culture, manners. “Living in our society with diverse races, there are Malays, Chinese, Indians, Orang Asli, Ibans and Dayaks. “Should we feel a need to insult others because of their skin colour, because they have different beliefs, different cultures?” he asked. The students answered “no”, and Anwar said that was the attitude he wanted the next generation to carry forward. Earlier, Anwar said mastering AI should go hand in hand with developing good character and treating others with respect. He said children should build their knowledge through reading and cautioned against assuming they could master a subject in a minute using AI. He urged teachers and principals to draw up compulsory reading lists for students during the December school holidays.
75705e49ef1d1037: HONG KONG, Nov 25 — A year after one of the worst fires in Hong Kong’s history, survivors are still struggling with the aftermath of losing their loved ones and homes.
The blaze, which officials say was “unprecedented” in scale, displaced thousands, prompted a months-long investigation, and led the government to apologise.
AFP looks at what took place during the November 26, 2025 fire and the months that followed:
Impact
The fire at Wang Fuk Court apartment complex was the world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980.
The inferno left 168 dead and 79 injured, displacing about 4,600 residents.
Of those who died, 114 victims — or about 70 per cent — were aged 65 or older.
The injured suffered from inhalation injuries, burns, and heat exhaustion.
The fire spread to seven buildings within 90 minutes, while the blaze took 43 hours to be fully extinguished.
Asif Sohail Usmani, a fire engineering expert, told an inquiry hearing the velocity of the spread was unprecedented in the world’s history of major building fires.
Causes
Authorities investigating the fire found it “was most likely caused by a glowing source, likely a cigarette”.
The flames ignited paper materials on the flat roof outside and spread to combustible construction materials.
The buildings were undergoing maintenance work at the time and most exterior walls were covered with non-fire-retardant scaffolding nets that helped to spread the blaze.
Fire alarm systems for seven of eight blocks had been deactivated, and water was turned off to the fire hoses.
Some of the victims had been trapped in escape routes, making firefighting and rescue efforts more challenging.
Survivors and residents
Many lingering issues remain unresolved for surviving former residents.

Several of them told AFP that over the past year they have faced immense psychological stress when dealing with property rights, relocations, and returning to their damaged homes to collect belongings.
Some who lost loved ones told local media that they have needed psychiatric treatment to combat depression.
Most residents accepted a buyout offer implemented by government, but many describe it as a “forced” choice that brings with it heavy debt for years to come.
The government has rejected a proposal to rebuild the complex, despite some residents’ calls, saying it would take nearly a decade.
Official response
The fire was caused by a “perfect storm” of issues and exposed the gaps in Hong Kong’s fire safety regulations at building sites, authorities said in an inquiry report.

Four government bodies — Housing Bureau’s independent checking unit, the fire services department, the labour department and the buildings department — “bear part of the responsibility”, said the report.
Regulators were “deceived” by contractors, who “are the main culprits” for the inferno and the high fatalities, officials said.
At least 40 people were arrested as of October as part of a criminal investigation into the fire, police told AFP.
Of those, 22 were arrested on suspicion of “manslaughter” and “fraud”.
Authorities also arrested, in the name of national security, some activists who were demanding accountability in a move that has been widely condemned.
Accountability
Nearly a year after the fire, Hong Kong leaders bowed in apology before reporters, and one minister resigned in response.
An “administrative accountability” is still underway.
Officials are also looking to tighten building codes and crack down on bid-rigging — a practice believed to be misused by contractors to obtain project licences.
But many residents said the apology and measures came too little and too late.
The tragic fire exposed “the banality of evil within the bureaucratic system”, former housing bureau chief Anthony Cheung told AFP.
That bureaucrats are “too risk-averse” as the inquiry found they were “shrinking responsibility”, Cheung added.
John Burns, a public administration professor, told AFP that “Hong Kong’s siloed governance arrangements have long struggled with poor coordination and weak accountability”.
“Citizens see incompetence” from authorities in regard to the fire, he said. — AFP
087369b8604a3dff: PETALING JAYA: Tiga pelajar yang tular memukul rakan sekelas dalam kejadian buli di sebuah sekolah menengah di Tangkak, didakwa di Mahkamah Majistret hari ini.
Semua pelajar lelaki berusia 15 tahun itu membuat pengakuan salah terhadap pertuduhan yang dibacakan di hadapan Majistret Arthana Sarma Rao, menurut Berita Harian.
Berdasarkan kertas pertuduhan, mereka bersama-sama didakwa dengan sengaja mencederakan rakan sekelas berusia 15 tahun dengan menendang dan menumbuk mangsa menggunakan tangan dan kaki.
Mereka didakwa melakukan perbuatan itu di sebuah sekolah menengah antara 8 pagi hingga 10.15 pagi, 13 November lalu.
Dakwaan dibuat mengikut Seksyen 323 Kanun Keseksaan yang dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 kanun sama.
Bagi pesalah juvana, mahkamah boleh memerintahkan mereka dilepas dengan amaran, dikenakan bon berkelakuan baik dengan syarat tertentu, membayar denda atau menjalani perintah khidmat masyarakat.
Mahkamah juga boleh memerintahkan pesalah dihantar ke Sekolah Henry Gurney, tertakluk kepada peruntukan undang-undang berkaitan.
Mengikut laporan ibu mangsa, anaknya berada dalam kelas sebelum dibelasah dan ditumbuk oleh ketiga-tiga pelajar terbabit.
Polis menerima laporan berhubung kejadian itu pada jam 12.09 tengah malam, 14 November lalu.
Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Lee Wee Hong mengendalikan pendakwaan manakala ketiga-tiga tertuduh tidak diwakili peguam.
Mahkamah membenarkan jaminan RM1,200 terhadap semua tertuduh sementara menunggu sebutan laporan akhlak daripada Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat (JKM), selain fakta dan perintah pada 23 Disember ini.
0c5adfd08ec78828: PETALING JAYA: Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) memfailkan dua saman terhadap Google LLC dengan tuntutan ganti rugi keseluruhan RM600 juta berhubung dakwaan kegagalan syarikat itu menangani kandungan dalam talian yang memudaratkan di platform YouTube.
Dalam kenyataan, MCMC kedua-dua saman itu melibatkan dakwaan berbeza berkaitan kegagalan Google mematuhi kewajipan di bawah undang-undang serta syarat lesen yang ditetapkan.
Bagi setiap saman, MCMC menuntut ganti rugi RM300 juta merangkumi RM100 juta ganti rugi am, RM100 juta ganti rugi teruk dan RM100 juta ganti rugi teladan.

“Tuntutan ganti rugi ini bertujuan mendapatkan pampasan atas penggunaan sumber dan tenaga kerja yang besar dalam menangani lebih daripada 50,000 kandungan dalam talian yang memudaratkan susulan kegagalan sistemik Google, di samping menyokong usaha mewujudkan persekitaran dalam talian yang lebih selamat.
“Tuntutan ini turut mengambil kira sifat dan kesan pelanggaran yang didakwa, serta keperluan untuk memastikan Google dipertanggungjawabkan atas ketidakpatuhan yang sama daripada berulang,” katanya.
Saman pertama berkaitan dakwaan kegagalan Google mengambil tindakan sewajarnya terhadap ribuan kandungan memudaratkan, termasuk perjudian dalam talian, penipuan dan scam.
MCMC berkata, antara 1 Jan hingga 28 Okt lalu pihaknya mengemukakan 74,703 laporan kepada YouTube, dengan 74,569 daripadanya atau 99.8% berkaitan perjudian dalam talian.
Daripada jumlah itu, 32,781 laporan menerima maklum balas atau tindakan penurunan kandungan dalam tempoh sehari, manakala 4,950 laporan tidak menerima sebarang maklum balas.
Sebanyak 35 laporan pula mengambil masa lebih 90 hari untuk menerima maklum balas atau tindakan penurunan kandungan, manakala 1,468 laporan mengambil masa lebih 30 hari.
“Angka-angka ini menunjukkan skala penyebaran kandungan yang memudaratkan di platform tersebut serta kelewatan dalam menangani kandungan berkenaan,” katanya.

Saman kedua pula membabitkan dakwaan kegagalan Google mengambil langkah statutori dan proaktif sewajarnya berhubung penerbitan semula kandungan yang melanggar undang-undang di YouTube oleh Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris atau lebih dikenali sebagai Papagomo.
MCMC berkata, kandungan berkenaan kini tertakluk kepada injunksi interim yang diperintahkan Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur pada 19 Jun lalu.

Suruhanjaya itu menegaskan, semua penyedia platform media sosial yang tertakluk kepada Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia 1998 serta Akta Keselamatan Dalam Talian 2025 perlu mematuhi kewajipan undang-undang dan syarat lesen masing-masing.
“Memandangkan ini bukan kes sivil pertama yang dibawa oleh MCMC terhadap syarikat media sosial utama berhubung pelanggaran seumpamanya.
“MCMC menggesa semua penyedia platform supaya mengambil langkah yang sewajarnya untuk menangani kandungan yang melanggar undang-undang dan memudaratkan di platform masing-masing,” katanya.
8d6db090defa8e07: TUMPAT, Nov 25 — The air force pilot detained over the 96.6kg methamphetamine find at Subang Air Base acted as both coordinator and “transporter” for the drug syndicate, police said today.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the pilot is among 13 people arrested over the seizure, which is worth RM4.83 million, Harian Metro reported.

“The pilot who was detained acted as a coordinator and also a ‘transporter’ to bring the drug supply from the Klang Valley to Sabah,” he was quoted as telling reporters after visiting the family of the late lance corporal Muhammad Shahrul Aliff Yaacob, who died in a crash involving a police van in Sungkai, Perak, on November 17.
The drugs were found during a routine luggage check at Subang Air Base in Selangor on November 17, when five bags and a box were seized.
Early investigations show the syndicate moved drugs from Subang to Labuan and Tawau, though police have not ruled out other destinations, Hussein said.
He said every member of a syndicate has a role, and the arrests so far involve only some of them.
Of the 13 detained, seven are Royal Malaysian Air Force officers and personnel, and six are civilians.
Hussein said police had identified several syndicate members before making the arrests, and some other individuals have been singled out for further action.
“How much they were paid is still under investigation and we cannot reveal it yet,” he said.
He added that how many trips were made using military assets is also being investigated.
“Give police room to complete the investigation, after which the inspector-general of police will share the findings,” he said.
2e51875a7e8351f0: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysia has identified 274,887 metric tonnes of surveyed rare earth element (REE) resources as of 2025, following exploration studies conducted by the Department of Minerals and Geoscience (JMG).

Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said efforts to increase the level of confidence in the nation’s REE resource estimates will continue through a second phase of the REE resource potential assessment project, under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) for the 2026—2030 period.
He noted that the project, with an allocation of RM38.49 million, covers an assessment area of 160 square kilometres across 10 states.

“For 2026, RM9 million has been allocated for the assessment of a 30 km² area across six states and as of October 2026, the target area for assessment has been fully covered,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Arthur was responding to a question from Salamiah Mohd Nor (PN-Temerloh) regarding the government’s plans to develop the nation’s REE resources in a controlled and sustainable manner including inquiries into which states hold the largest REE deposits, estimated reserves, economic value, mining methods, and environmental monitoring mechanisms.

He added that, based on preliminary surveys by JMG, Malaysia is estimated to possess 16.1 million tonnes of REE resources, with the largest deposits identified in Terengganu, Kelantan, Perak, Pahang, and Kedah.
“However, these figures represent estimated mineral resources rather than mineral reserves that have been verified as commercially viable for mining.

“Malaysia should not rely solely on its wealth of mineral resources; instead, it must master the necessary technology and develop the entire industrial value chain to maximise economic returns for the nation and its people,” he said.

In a related development, he noted that a collaboration between Lynas Rare Earths and South Korea’s JS Link Incorporated formalised through a long-term partnership agreement worth RM1 billion last July has led to the development of a permanent magnet manufacturing plant in Kuantan, Pahang.
The plant is designed with an annual production capacity of 3,000 metric tonnes and has the potential to create up to 700 new jobs.

Meanwhile, Arthur said Malaysia intends to leverage Asean cooperation to strengthen the nation’s critical mineral industrial value chain by facilitating investments, expanding market access, and fostering the sharing of technology and expertise.

“Previously, the Asean Ministerial Meeting on Minerals (AMMin) was held only once every three years. However, starting this year with Malaysia as the host, the meeting will be held annually, allowing all Asean member states to place greater emphasis on the development of the regional mineral sector,” he said.

He added that the government would ensure that the agreements reached during the 11th AMMin, held in the capital yesterday, are translated into a development strategy for the nation’s critical mineral industry. — Bernama
a8a23fa11b8bf68f: PETALING JAYA: Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen today slammed the state PKR chapter's decision to sit out the Dec 12 election.
Chong claimed that the move was aimed at securing continued support for the federal government from Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS), and reflected the influence wielded by the ruling coalition.
"To me, this is sacrificing democracy in Sarawak for political support at the federal level," he said in a Facebook live video.
Chong said Sarawak DAP had the autonomy to decide what was best for the state, adding that a stronger opposition was needed to keep GPS in check.
"Elections must not be seen as a destabilising force in any democratic society, but rather to reinforce the notion of checks and balances. Otherwise, there is no need for any election," he said.
He also said DAP had stood the test of time as an opposition party in Sarawak, pointing to assemblymen from local opposition parties who eventually joined the ruling coalition.
"We must always bear in mind that absolute power corrupts absolutely. We need a stronger opposition to provide the necessary checks and balances on GPS," he said.
Sarawak PKR announced yesterday that it would not contest the state election, citing its cooperation and commitment with GPS in the unity government.
Amanah has also decided to opt out of the polls, leaving DAP as the only Pakatan Harapan component party in the contest. DAP is set to clash with GPS in 12 out of 82 seats.
Nomination day is on Nov 28, with polling on Dec 12. Early voting is on Dec 8.
d0f7b98a89725fe7: SHAH ALAM: A man failed in his appeal before the High Court here today to set aside his convictions for sexually assaulting his co-tenant's daughter five years ago.

Judicial Commissioner Helina Sulaiman dismissed the 54-year-old's appeal against his convictions on two charges under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act and upheld the sentences imposed by the sessions court last year.

According to the facts of the case, the man, who was ordered to serve a total of seven years in prison for both charges and receive four strokes of the rotan, lived with the girl's family in a rented house in Ampang.
Between Dec 10 and 15, 2021, the man sexually assaulted the then 12-year-old girl in the kitchen by touching her inappropriately after showing her adult videos, and told her "not to tell mama".
The girl's mother lodged a police report after the girl told her about the incidents.

In upholding the convictions, Helina said there was no reason to disturb the lower court's findings, adding that the girl was a credible witness because she explained what happened on both days using anatomically detailed dolls.
"There is no reason for a child to make up stories that she was assaulted as claimed by the defence," she said.

The judge said the seven-year jail terms for both charges, to be served concurrently, were neither excessive nor insufficient. "The sentences imposed were within the statutory limit under the law," she said.
a22e7915c97cf92a: GEORGE TOWN: The Region 1 Marine Police Force (PPM) crippled a transnational drug smuggling syndicate operating through sea routes with the seizure of over 103kg of methamphetamine worth RM5.36 million and the arrest of four men during recent operations in the waters off Tanjung Dawai and Sungai Petani, Kedah.

Bukit Aman internal security and public order department director Yusri Hassan Basri said the team, which was on patrol at 9pm on Nov 14, encountered a fibreglass boat about seven nautical miles from Pulau Sayak in the waters off Tanjung Dawai.
"When instructed to stop for inspection, the boat sped off and made several dangerous manoeuvres in a bid to evade capture.

"However, our team managed to intercept the boat after a 90-minute high-speed chase, and we arrested two Indonesian men who were on board," he told a press conference at the Region One PPM headquarters here today.
The press conference was also attended by Bukit Aman PPM commander Shamsol Kassim.

Yusri said an inspection of the boat led to the discovery of five white sacks containing 100 gold-coloured plastic packets labelled "VIP 666" filled with 103kg of methamphetamine estimated to be worth RM5.36 million, concealed in a specially constructed compartment.
Following the arrests, police raided a house in Kampung Sungai Layar Hujung, Sungai Petani, and detained two more men – a Malaysian and an Indonesian – on Nov 15.

"The 36-year-old Malaysian suspect, who is self-employed and runs a grocery shop, is believed to be the mastermind behind the drug trafficking syndicate, planning and coordinating the drug shipments as well as offering RM12,000 for each trip to transport the drugs to Indonesia.

"Further investigations found that the two men were believed to have made six trips to smuggle drugs from Malaysia to a neighbouring country via sea routes to avoid detection by the authorities," he said.
While the three Indonesian suspects had valid passports, Yusri said they were believed to have entered the country through unofficial entry points to carry out the drug smuggling activities.
Police also seized the fibreglass boat and a Toyota Hilux four-wheel drive vehicle. Yusri said the seized drugs could feed the habit of 518,990 addicts.

He said further investigations were ongoing, including efforts to trace the syndicate’s distribution network. All four suspects, aged between 31 and 36, are being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
The operation involved one officer and 18 personnel from the Region One PPM, with support from the marine intelligence unit and patrol boats PSC 45, PSC 60 and PIB 01.
Yusri said Region One PPM recorded 151 drug-related cases from January to November this year, resulting in 180 arrests and the seizure of illicit substances worth RM11.96 million.
In total, 2,375 cases were recorded, with 1,462 arrests and seizures, including forfeitures, valued at RM187.99 million.
b1622127bcee21fc: PUTRAJAYA: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim sekali lagi memberi bayangan bahawa beliau tidak merancang mengadakan PRU lebih awal, dengan berkata kerajaan pimpinannya masih mempunyai 'lebih setahun' sebelum tamat penggal.

bd27918a836a2e64: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan akan mengekalkan dasar dwirangkaian 5G negara, kata Menteri Komunikasi Fahmi Fadzil.

Kedua-dua rangkaian itu menggunakan teknologi berbeza dengan Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) menggunakan peralatan Ericsson, manakala U Mobile selaku pengendali rangkaian kedua menggunakan teknologi Huawei dan ZTE.
Fahmi berkata, dasar itu bukan sahaja memberi keyakinan kepada pelbagai pihak untuk berkomunikasi dengan selamat menggunakan peralatan daripada penyedia teknologi tertentu.
Malah menurutnya, ia membolehkan satu rangkaian menjadi alternatif kepada rangkaian lain sekiranya berlaku kecemasan.

“Sekiranya apa-apa berlaku kepada satu rangkaian, maka rangkaian kedua boleh diaktifkan,” katanya dalam sidang media selepas merasmikan NEXSEC 2026 di Pusat Pameran dan Perdagangan Antarabangsa Malaysia (Mitec).

Fahmi berkata, beliau sudah meminta kedua-dua pengendali mengadakan perbincangan bagi membolehkan pengguna terus mendapat perkhidmatan daripada rangkaian alternatif jika rangkaian mereka mengalami gangguan.
Katanya, langkah itu bertujuan mengelakkan risiko perkhidmatan kepada pengguna terputus akibat kegagalan satu rangkaian.

Hala tuju dasar dwirangkaian 5G negara menjadi perhatian susulan rancangan perubahan struktur pemilikan DNB, dengan kerajaan dijangka tidak lagi menjadi pemegang saham utama, manakala CelcomDigi, Maxis dan YTL Power bakal memperoleh kawalan lebih besar.

Perkembangan itu mencetuskan kebimbangan dalam kalangan penganalisis sama ada kepelbagaian teknologi antara kedua-dua rangkaian dapat dikekalkan, terutama jika keputusan perolehan pada masa depan membawa kepada penggunaan teknologi yang semakin serupa.
Pada 12 Nov lalu, EuroCham Malaysia berkata kejelasan dan konsistensi dasar 5G negara mampu meningkatkan keyakinan pelabur asing dalam membuat keputusan perniagaan jangka panjang.

Ketua Pegawai Eksekutifnya Kati Ferry berkata pendekatan Malaysia menggunakan teknologi Barat dan China memberi kelebihan daya saing kepada negara, selain membolehkan syarikat memilih rangkaian yang bersesuaian dengan keperluan operasi masing-masing.
46fdf560b45aa63e: KUALA LUMPUR: A Libyan university student was charged in the magistrates’ court here today with reckless driving, causing the death of a retired soldier in an accident on Jalan Jelatek last weekend.
Ali Abdul Rahman Mahmoud Elmaki, 32, pleaded not guilty to the charge after it was read to him before magistrate Amalina Johar.
He is accused of driving a Proton Saga in a reckless and dangerous manner, causing the death of Hairezam Omar, 43, on Jalan Jelatek heading towards Taman Keramat at 1am on Nov 21.
The charge, framed under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, carries a jail term of between five and 10 years and a fine of up to RM50,000 upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Fadhly Zamry opposed bail, citing the gravity of the offence and Elmaki’s status as a foreign national.
However, he said the prosecution would leave the matter to the court’s discretion under Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code, proposing bail of RM70,000 with two Malaysian sureties.

The prosecution also sought additional conditions, including for Elmaki to surrender his passport to the court, report to a nearby police station monthly and have his driving licence suspended until the case is disposed of.
Fadhly said the conditions were necessary because Elmaki was a foreign national and posed a flight risk.
Defence counsel K Ramalingam asked for bail of RM10,000, saying his client was pursuing a master’s degree and had examinations next month. He denied that his client was a flight risk.
"My client lives in Malaysia with his wife and has a permanent address on Jalan Ampang. He is ready to comply with all the additional conditions proposed by the prosecution," he said.
The court granted bail of RM17,000 with two Malaysian sureties and imposed the additional conditions sought by the prosecution.
The case was fixed for mention on Jan 28.
b2ff963335fa592c: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has again signalled that he is not planning to call an early general election, saying his government has "more than a year left" in its term.
When asked whether there was still time for his administration to do more after four years in office, Anwar said the government would "do our best and improve our performance".
"We have more than a year left," he told reporters after launching the AI Temu AI programme at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre today.

Deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also Umno president and Barisan Nasional chairman, previously said that dissolving Parliament to seek a fresh mandate would be better than a Cabinet reshuffle, following Loke Siew Fook’s resignation as transport minister.
Loke resigned on Nov 10 over the issue of house arrest for former prime minister Najib Razak.
The current Dewan Rakyat's term is due to expire in December 2027 unless dissolved earlier.
When asked about Loke’s status in the Cabinet, Anwar reiterated that he had yet to accept Loke's resignation, adding that he recently met with the DAP secretary-general.
"He gave his reasons. I told him to go on leave first," he said.
On how the transport ministry’s duties would be handled in the meantime, Anwar said its secretary-general and deputy minister could oversee its operations.
3c480a030749f4c3: SINGAPORE: US-listed exchange-traded funds investing in Bitcoin are heading for the worst month of outflows since their 2024 debut, as a persistent selloff in the world’s largest cryptocurrency drives investors away.

A net US$4.71 billion has been withdrawn from the funds in November so far, according to data compiled by Bloomberg through Nov 23. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, the largest fund holding the token, has suffered about US$4 billion of redemptions this month, also putting it on course for its worst monthly outflow.

The exodus comes as Bitcoin tumbles below US$60,000 and heads for its worst monthly performance since June 2022, when a string of corporate failures triggered a broader crypto-market meltdown. The token has dropped about 23% this month and was trading around US$59,200 as of 1pm Wednesday in Singapore, down about 1% in the Asia session.

The losses underscore a sharp reversal for a group of ETFs that helped propel Bitcoin higher after their US debut in January 2024. The funds opened the cryptocurrency to a wider pool of institutional and retail investors and became an important source of demand during the bull market. Their record redemptions are now reinforcing the current downturn as that source of buying dries up.

Bitcoin briefly recovered alongside other risk assets on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, but has since surrendered all of those gains, a sign that investors are using rallies to reduce exposure.

“When a market cannot hold a rally on good news, it usually means that investors are using any strength to sell,” data analytics firm Glassnode said in a note. “Bitcoin trades around the clock and tends to be one of the first assets sold when investors want less risk.”

Bitcoin is facing numerous headwinds at the moment, from high-profile hacks that have undermined confidence in its security to the prospect of higher interest rates and greater regulatory scrutiny following recent US midterm elections. The absence of US demand is adding to the pressure, according to Glassnode.

“The ETFs and other institutions were an important source of demand on the way up, and there is little interest from them at these prices,” the firm said. “A return to ETF inflows, together with net buying on Coinbase, would be the first sign that this is changing.”

Bitcoin is also facing greater competition for investor capital as money gravitates toward equities and assets offering income, according to Ayesha Kiani, chief operating officer of Monarq Asset Management.
Bitcoin is “competing for the same risk capital that is going into equities right now,” Kiani told Bloomberg Television, describing the ETF exodus as “concerning.”
The cryptocurrency industry may need a fresh catalyst to revive demand after the forces that drove the previous rally have faded, she said.

“I think we do need to find a new narrative, a new catalyst, a new market, something new for the entire industry for us to become that emerging asset class again,” Kiani said. “There are better yield-bearing assets out there at this point. So, like, why Bitcoin?”
ee4934531afeae2a: KUALA LUMPUR: Urusan pengisytiharan anggapan kematian 54 rakyat Malaysia yang hilang dalam tragedi banjir di Nepal tertakluk sepenuhnya kepada prosedur perundangan dan mekanisme pentadbiran negara itu, kata Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

Beliau berkata, Jabatan Pendaftaran Negara (JPN) hanya boleh mengeluarkan sijil kematian rasmi di bawah Akta Pendaftaran Kelahiran dan Kematian 1957 (Akta 299) selepas pihak berkuasa di lokasi insiden mengeluarkan pengesahan terlebih dahulu.

Bagaimanapun, katanya kerajaan Nepal telah meluluskan satu perintah eksekutif dikenali Ordinan Pengisytiharan Kematian Mangsa Bencana hasil komunikasi Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim dengan rakan sejawatnya di negara berkenaan.
“Dengan pindaan administratif ini, anggapan kematian sebelum Kerajaan Nepal keluarkan sijil mati, asalnya (mengambil masa) 12 tahun. Tetapi dengan pindaan itu, dipendekkan kepada 45 hari sahaja.

“Jadi, bila pengesahan itu datang daripada kerajaan Nepal ke atas 54 orang (rakyat Malaysia) ini, JPN akan menyusul untuk mengeluarkan sijil kematian bagi memudahkan urusan para waris melakukan proses berikutnya,” katanya pada sesi soal jawab di Dewan Rakyat.

Beliau menjawab soalan Muhammad Bakhtiar Wan Chik (PH-Balik Pulau) yang meminta penjelasan status terkini sijil anggapan kematian, selain bantuan kewangan segera kepada keluarga mangsa yang kehilangan pencari nafkah utama dalam kejadian banjir tersebut.
Bagaimanapun, Saifuddin berkata kelancaran proses itu bergantung kepada kerjasama waris dalam melengkapkan dokumentasi diperlukan mengikut prosedur negara berkenaan.
"Kerjasama daripada keluarga mangsa itu adalah prasyarat yang penting. Selesai urusan itu lagi cepat, cepatlah (pengisytiharan anggapan kematian) melibatkan 54 orang ini," katanya.

Menjawab soalan tambahan Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) sama ada kerajaan bersedia memperkenalkan mekanisme dokumentasi bencana laluan pantas (fast-track) seperti diamalkan Thailand, Saifuddin Nasution berkata prosedur sedia ada JPN sudah memadai.

Beliau berkata, bagi kematian biasa di luar negara, JPN hanya mengambil masa tujuh hari bekerja untuk mengeluarkan sijil kematian sebaik dokumen pengesahan diterima, selain turut mempermudahkan urusan menerusi borang alternatif sekiranya waris tidak memiliki kad pengenalan si mati.

“Pada pandangan saya, mekanisme sedia ada memadai bagi kategori kematian biasa di luar negara kerana waris hanya perlu mengemukakan dokumen pengenalan diri dan pengesahan kematian daripada negara berkenaan kepada JPN sebelum sijil kematian dikeluarkan dalam tempoh tujuh hari bekerja.

“Sebab itu saya sebut dalam kes ini, kita mengambil ketetapan, kita akan patuh terhadap ordinan yang berkuat kuasa di Nepal dalam melaksanakan ataupun mengesahkan satu-satu insiden kematian,” katanya.
Katanya, kerajaan akan sentiasa mengambil pengajaran daripada setiap musibah yang berlaku untuk memperkemas prosedur di samping mengeratkan lagi kerjasama dengan negara lain.
Pada 26 Ogos lepas, banjir kilat melanda daerah Rasuwa di Nepal serta kawasan sempadan Nepal-Tibet susulan runtuhan ais glasier dan batuan di kawasan tadahan hulu Lhende Khola di Tibet.
Tragedi itu meragut lebih 1,400 nyawa dengan kira-kira 5,700 individu termasuk lebih 600 warga asing masih dilaporkan hilang.

b7c590fbfe359b66: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) plans to expand its fleet from 101 to 129 aircraft by 2035 as part of its long-term growth strategy.
MAG president and group CEO Nasaruddin A Bakar said the fleet would include aircraft operated by Malaysia Airlines, Firefly and the group's cargo operations.

He was speaking after a document exchange ceremony for MAG's long-range widebody aircraft acquisition today, during which the group announced the purchase of 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, with an option to purchase six more, to gradually replace its seven Airbus A350-900 aircraft.
The new aircraft, powered by GE Aerospace's GEnx engines, will be delivered between 2032 and 2035, by which time the A350s will be about 13 to 15 years old.

Nasaruddin said the catalogue value of all 16 aircraft, including their engines, was US$9.3 billion (RM38.28 billion). He said MAG would consider various financing options, including sale-and-leaseback arrangements, operating leases and finance leases.

He said while the Dreamliners would offer greater fuel efficiency and support the group's target of about 5% annual growth, MAG cut about 6% of its planned capacity this year because of higher fuel costs, despite having increased capacity by 12% year-on-year. "We are growing at a disciplined pace," he said.
The aircraft are expected to serve routes including London, Paris, Sydney, Melbourne, Tokyo and Seoul. Nasaruddin said MAG was also preparing contingency plans for aircraft delivery delays.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, who witnessed the ceremony, said rising fuel prices and geopolitical uncertainty continued to challenge the aviation industry, as airlines still had to pay commercial fuel prices despite the government keeping RON95 petrol prices low for Malaysians.
Anwar also praised Malaysia Airlines staff for their service and reaffirmed the government's commitment to the national carrier.
"We’ll do whatever is necessary to ensure that Malaysia Airlines can re-emerge as a great player in the aviation industry," he said.

0c784a9a8ad64029: PETALING JAYA: Sindiket penipuan dalam talian mengaut RM7.33 bilion daripada mangsa di Malaysia antara 2023 hingga bulan lalu, menurut Kementerian Dalam Negeri.
Menteri Dalam Negeri, Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, berkata polis merekodkan 192,869 kes sepanjang tempoh itu, yang membawa kepada 75,266 individu ditahan dan 69,665 orang didakwa.
Menurutnya, dalam tempoh 10 bulan pertama tahun ini saja, sebanyak 56,802 kes direkodkan dengan jumlah kerugian mencecah RM1.56 bilion.

Menjawab soalan V Ganabatirau (PH-Klang) di Dewan Rakyat, beliau berkata, skim pelaburan mencatatkan jumlah kerugian tertinggi sejak 2023, iaitu RM3.4 bilion, diikuti penipuan telekomunikasi RM2.13 bilion dan penipuan beli-belah dalam talian sebanyak RM509 juta.
Jelasnya, enam daripada 10 mangsa penipuan dalam talian terdiri daripada wanita, manakala pekerja sektor swasta ialah kumpulan mangsa terbesar.

Dalam tempoh sama, polis mengesan 254,546 akaun keldai, iaitu akaun bank yang digunakan untuk menerima dan memindahkan wang hasil kegiatan penipuan. Sebahagian besar akaun itu didapati milik pelajar yang membenarkan penipu menggunakannya.
Saifuddin berkata, sindiket penipuan hanya memerlukan lima minit untuk memindahkan wang melalui beberapa akaun sebelum mengeluarkannya.
"Panggilan pertama daripada mangsa sangat penting," katanya sambil menggesa mangsa penipuan segera menghubungi Pusat Respons Scam Kebangsaan (NSRC) di talian 997.
Beliau berkata, NSRC menerima 30,000 panggilan sepanjang bulan lalu saja, dengan purata 1,000 panggilan sehari, yang sebahagiannya akibat peningkatan kesedaran orang ramai.

c33bcd47cf0102df: VMware has issued its third critical security advisory in a week, this time to warn of four critical flaws and address a total of 23 issues.
VMSA-2026-0011 landed on November 24, just five days after two other advisories. VMware’s FAQ for the new advisory includes the following remarks:
Because of coordinated disclosure and release pipeline timing this VMSA comes on the heels of VMSA-2026-0009, and atop a major holiday in the United States.

The security vulnerability landscape is more dynamic than ever; please know that while we acknowledge this timing is not optimal, your ability to operate and maintain a secure environment amidst modern, AI-assisted threats is paramount to us.

Make of that what you will as you ponder how and when to patch the four critical flaws, including the 9.8-rated CVE-2026-123903, which allows a malicious actor to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to vCenter, the management tool VMware users rely on to manage hosts and VMs.
This is the third 9.8-rated authentication issue VMware has fixed in vCenter since July.

Two of the other critical flaws in this new advisory allow an attacker to run code on an ESX host, earning the bugs a 9.8 rating. CVE-2026-123910 makes that possible thanks to a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the I/O filter service, while CVE-2026-123911 is a use-after-free vulnerability.

The other critical flaw, CVE-2026-123912, can result in a guest escape from VMware’s desktop Workstation and Fusion desktop hypervisors. It’s also present in VMware’s ESX hypervisor, but attackers thankfully can’t escape that product’s sandbox. This one’s easy to mitigate because the problem is in a USB controller that users can turn off.
Most of the other flaws require installation of updated software.

There’s a little good news in that some of the software updates VMware issued last week include fixes for the newly disclosed flaws. But there are still plenty of fresh fixes to apply, across ten products: ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, VMware tools, Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, the Telco Cloud Platform, Telco Cloud Infrastructure, and the VMware Avi Load Balancer.

VMware’s advisory thanks external researchers for finding and reporting most of the flaws. The Broadcom business unit is known to be a member of Project Glasswing, the Anthropic-run effort to use the Mythos model to find flaws that has seen many vendors dramatically increase the number of patches they produce.

In past years, VMware has often published considerably more than this year’s 11 security advisories. With five weeks left in the year, perhaps vAdmins need to worry Christmas might also get complicated. ®

51cef91e1b59ebe9: HONG KONG: Xiaomi’s shares soared more than 8% after smartphone sales held up better than anticipated, suggesting the Chinese company was succeeding in a move up-market to offset memory chip costs.

The company’s stock rose their most in nearly three weeks after reporting flat September-quarter smartphone revenue, beating projections for a 6% decline. Xiaomi managed a record, near-40% surge in the average selling price of its gadgets during the period, reflecting a shift toward premium phones less vulnerable to skyrocketing memory prices.

AI’s voracious demand for semiconductors created a dire shortage of conventional chips that’s now hitting consumer electronics makers around the globe. That’s compelled smartphone makers from Apple Inc. to Xiaomi to raise prices on their devices.

The latest Xiaomi 18 Fold, released at the end of the third quarter, is priced at more than 10,000 yuan (US$1,500) and is contending with Apple’s iPhone Duo and similar gadgets from Huawei in the high-end segment.

“Memory cost pressure will likely persist into 2027, but premiumization has been cushioning the impact,” Bernstein analyst Eunice Lee wrote in a research note. “The stock has traded largely inversely to memory and AI sentiment lately, which we expect to remain the key drivers of near-term price action.”

The Chinese maker of smartphones and cars posted a 5.2% drop in overall revenue in the three months ended September to 107.2 billion yuan, better than the 6% decline expected by analysts. Net income tumbled 68% to 3.9 billion yuan.
The electric vehicle and artificial intelligence division reported a loss of 3.4 billion yuan, which executives attributed to growing investments into AI during a post-earnings call on Tuesday.

The EV business has lost momentum as the wider China auto market contracts. The company delivered 100,975 vehicles in the third quarter, dropping 7% from to a year earlier. Executives reaffirmed the company’s target of entering the German market in the third quarter of 2027, saying recent EU trade barriers will not significantly affect its strategy for the bloc.
The company also launched a new line of hybrid sports utility vehicles in the third quarter. Robust initial demand for the SkyNomad is expected to help offset flagging electric-vehicle deliveries.

“The third quarter is the most difficult period I have experienced throughout my career in the industry, but Xiaomi has become more at ease in dealing with the challenge,” president Lu Weibing told media following the release of results. “We’ll constantly adjust our pricing and find a balance between cushioning the impact of rising cost and ensuring consumer acceptance.”
9ee484497e4a362a: DHAKA, Nov 25 — Bangladesh’s garment workers won a 36 per cent minimum wage increase today, officials said, after weeks of sometimes violent protests causing hundreds of millions of dollars in business losses.
The South Asian nation, the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, has seen widespread demonstrations since October by workers demanding higher pay.

The garment industry, which clothes millions of consumers across Europe and North America, is Bangladesh’s economic lifeline, generating four-fifths of export earnings and employing more than four million people.
After the deal was struck following lengthy negotiations with factory owners, workers’ representatives urged people to return to factories.
“Although we are not completely satisfied, the outcome is not entirely bad either,” Babul Akhter, the labour representative on a wage board set up to resolve the crisis, told reporters.
“Previously, workers used to get a wage revision every five years, but this time they are getting a revised wage after three years.”
It was not immediately clear how workers — who clashed with police in industrial zones yesterday — would react to the deal.
Workers initially demanded a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka (RM1,000), up from 12,500 taka.
They say their pay has failed to keep pace with the rising cost of food, housing, transport and health care.
Judge Syed Azad Subhani, the chairman of the government-appointed garment industry wage board, said the “majority supported a minimum wage of 17,000 taka”, after a vote early today.
The wage hike will take effect in January.
‘Export engine’

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said on Sunday that protests had cost the industry an estimated US$428 million in losses, while orders worth US$254 million had shifted to other countries.
The disruption came ahead of the busy Christmas season.
The garment industry, which supplies major international brands including Fruit of the Loom and Levi Strauss, earns around US$38 billion a year.
Bangladesh supplies more than 150 countries with ready-made garments, according to the BGMEA, which represents around 4,000 factories.
The United States is its biggest individual market, while the European Union is its largest trading bloc.
When Bangladesh won independence from Pakistan in 1971, it was among the world’s poorest countries, with its economy devastated by war.
The expansion of garment production helped transform the nation of around 170 million people from a predominantly agricultural economy into a major global manufacturing hub.
Bangladesh’s central bank calls the garment sector the “country’s export engine”.
But its success has been built on a vast, relatively low-paid workforce, with longstanding disputes over wages, working conditions and labour rights.

The 2013 Rana Plaza factory collapse, which killed more than 1,100 people and injured thousands, exposed appalling safety conditions in the industry, with workers employed in dangerous buildings and often lacking adequate labour protections.

The disaster prompted major international efforts to improve workplace standards, including an agreement between global clothing brands and trade unions to inspect factories and enforce safety measures. — AFP

f38105e96259c3cb: HONG KONG, Nov 25 — Technology firms once again tumbled today as the euphoria that greeted the return of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was washed away by the now-common panic and uncertainty over the AI boom.

News that the poster child of the artificial intelligence explosion had returned less than two weeks after resigning over extramarital affairs — including with an alleged Chinese spy — sent Asian markets into a swoon yesterday.
Traders were reassured about the ongoing presence of a fixer and visionary to an industry that has fuelled a tech revolution and a global economic boom.

But the mood appeared to have already soured as analysts pointed to the reality that there were still huge worries about the colossal sums pumped into the AI buildout and when they would see returns, if any.
After explosive gains yesterday, Asian stock markets were back in the doldrums.
Taipei, Tokyo and Seoul — home of most of the region’s key AI-linked firms — sank 8 per cent, more than 3 per cent and more than 5 per cent, respectively.
That came a day after surging 9 per cent, 3.9 per cent and more than 6 per cent respectively.
The losses were led by Taiwan’s TSMC and MediaTek, Japanese chip giants Kioxia and Advantest, and South Korean titans SK hynix and Samsung.
There was also heavy selling in Shanghai, Sydney and Singapore. However, Hong Kong, Wellington and Manila edged up.

The rout followed a return to reality on Wall Street, where Nvidia — which had rocketed more than 31 per cent Monday — shed almost 6 per cent, while AI giant Anthropic lost 6.5 per cent to fall below last week’s US$83 (RM341.30) IPO price.
AMD, Intel and Micron also took a hammering after the previous day’s surge.
The Nasdaq shed 1.5 per cent and the S&P 500 lost 0.5 per cent but the Dow rose, with analysts pointing out that traders were rotating into other sectors.
‘Dead-cat bounce’
“The champagne from (the) Nvidia resurrection had barely lost its fizz before Wall Street was back reaching for the sick bags,” said SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes.

“What looked like the mother of all relief rallies has already acquired the rather less flattering characteristics of a dead-cat bounce, with the Nasdaq taking another beating (and) Nvidia surrendering a sizeable chunk of its extraordinary gains.
He said “professional investors (were) apparently using the opening provided by the Jensen Huang comeback to unload technology exposure rather than rebuild it”.
“And that, unfortunately, is what happens when a market rallies on the back of forced buying rather than genuine conviction.”

And BNZ’s Jason Wong added: “Despite Huang’s return, some key issues continue to overhang the AI sector, including whether investment in the sector will provide an adequate return and the threat of regulation under a new administration from next year.”
Nvidia also remains under scrutiny from investigators including at the FBI and on Capitol Hill for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to the firm’s top-line chips.
Investors will be keeping an eye on the release of the Federal Reserve’s preferred gauge of inflation later in the day, which could play a role in its interest rate decision next month.
With price gains still far above target, officials are widely expected to hike, but their post-meeting statement will be pored over for an idea about the bank’s plans for the new year.

In company news, Chinese electronics giant Xiaomi jumped 8 per cent in Hong Kong on optimism for the performance of the company’s higher-end smartphones even as an AI-driven memory chip supply crunch hits profits. — AFP
3e6bca11ce95d356: Nutanix CEO Rajiv Ramaswami has decided to step down from the job once the company’s board can find his successor.

Ramaswami announced his decision on Tuesday and in conversation with The Register said he doesn’t have another job lined up, isn’t sure what he will do next, fancies sitting on boards or advising startups, but will take a break after Nutanix finds its next leader.

The CEO moved from VMware to Nutanix in 2020 and characterized his time at the company as writing its “second chapter.” The first, he explained, saw Nutanix focus on hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) and a limited group of workloads, especially desktop virtualization, while struggling to make a profit.

In chapter two, Nutanix redefined HCI as “hybrid cloud infrastructure” by enabling its stack to run on-prem or in public clouds, and by adding support for containers alongside VMs. Ramaswami took credit for stabilizing Nutanix’s finances while leading the expansion of its platform and for keeping net promoter scores high while the company grew.

The CEO added that Nutanix’s decision to end its devotion to virtualized storage and start to support external arrays was also part of chapter two. Ramaswami said he hopes to expand the number of storage vendors Nutanix supports beyond Dell, Everpure, and NetApp, until it works with all major array suppliers.
Chapter 3, he said, will be making Nutanix an AI platform, “by catering to a whole new set of ecosystems.”

Ramaswami told The Register he had been thinking about moving on for some time and raised it with the board in recent weeks. In the letter he wrote to Nutanix staff, the CEO said the company's board has begun the search for a successor and said he will remain at his post until a replacement is found and then “continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time.”

News of the CEO’s planned departure came on the same day Nutanix announced its Q1 results, which saw 15 percent revenue growth to $772.4 million. The company added 410 customers in the quarter, the slowest growth for several years. Ramaswami said high hardware costs remain “a headwind” for Nutanix, but said the company continues to win customers seeking an alternative to VMware. He also pointed to the largest new customer win for the quarter coming from a financial services outfit that uses Dell external storage, a significant score because two years ago Nutanix could not have competed for that business.

Nutanix forecast slightly faster growth for the rest of its financial year, suggesting it is not ready to ride AI’s rocket to riches. Investors knocked about ten percent off the company’s share price in after-hours trading, sending it to around $50, roughly double what it was when Ramaswami took over as CEO, but below $79-plus peaks in late 2025. ®

405805eeb8c19c97: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysia Airlines is set to replace its fleet of Airbus A350s with Boeing 787 Dreamliners, in a major overhaul of its long-haul operations aimed at increasing capacity and improving fuel efficiency.

The aircraft are scheduled for delivery between 2032 and 2035, when the group’s existing fleet of seven Airbus A350s is expected to be gradually phased out.
The deal will make Malaysia Airlines the first Malaysian carrier to operate the Dreamliner, although MAG did not disclose the value of the order or specify which 787 model it was acquiring.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim attended a signing ceremony in Kuala Lumpur, alongside representatives from Boeing, engine manufacturer GE Aerospace and sovereign wealth fund Khazanah Nasional Berhad.
MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the acquisition represented a strategic investment in the group’s future.

“As we look ahead to the next phase of growth, these aircraft will strengthen our ability to serve key international markets with greater capacity, efficiency and flexibility, while delivering the elevated travel experience our customers expect,” he said.
The Dreamliners will accommodate 319 passengers across three cabin classes, allowing Malaysia Airlines to deploy larger aircraft on selected long-haul routes and improve operating economics.

Powered by GE Aerospace’s GEnx-1B engines, the aircraft are expected to serve major destinations across Europe and the Asia-Pacific, including London, Paris, Sydney, Melbourne, Tokyo, Osaka and Seoul, subject to future network planning and operational requirements.
The acquisition further deepens MAG’s relationship with Boeing, which already supplies the backbone of Malaysia Airlines’ narrowbody fleet.
The national carrier currently operates more than 37 Boeing Next-Generation 737 aircraft alongside 19 Boeing 737-8s.

It has a total order book of 55 Boeing 737 aircraft, comprising 43 737-8s and 12 737-10s, through a combination of direct purchases and leasing arrangements, with the remaining aircraft expected to arrive by 2030.
