Pentas KLSCAH pernah digunakan dalam menuntut Akta Keselamatan Dalam Negeri dimansuhkan. Semasa Dr Mahathir Mohamad menentang Najib Razak bersabit skandal 1MDB, beliau bercakap di atas pentas KLSCAH.

Pemuda Umno memang ada 'sejarah tidak manis' dengan KLSCAH. Contoh: Pada 2001, Pemuda Umno mengadakan demonstrasi di hadapan bangunan KLSCAH bagi memprotes terhadap apa yang dikenali sebagai agenda 17 perkara yang diperjuangkan oleh Jawatankuasa Rayuan Pilihan Raya Pertubuhan Pertubuhan Cina Malaysia, yang lebih dikenali sebagai Suqiu.

Pemuda Umno tuduh Suqiu mempersoalkan hak keistimewaan orang Melayu. Suqiu menafikan. Pemuda Umno tetap berdemonstrasi di KLSCAH. Meskipun aman dengan kawalan polis, tetapi kata-kata kesat dan ancaman dilemparkan. Ertinya demonstrasi berbaur perkauman.
Jadi apabila Pemuda Umno zaman sekarang membantah soal premium bagi pembaharuan pajakan tanah KLSCAH, ia bukan sesuatu yang memeranjatkan. Bagi saya it's expected.

Meskipun banyak penjelasan telah diberi pelbagai pihak termasuk kerajaan khususnya Menteri Wilayah Persekutan Hannah Yeoh, Pemuda Umno dan golongan serta kumpulan sewaktu dengannya tidak berpuas hati. Ia dijadikan isu politik bersandar ras. Identity politics is alive and kicking. Sungguh sedih.

Saya tidak bercadang menghuraikan bantahan pihak yang membantah mahupun penjelasan pihak yang menjelaskan. Rasanya ramai yang sudah maklum. Saya cuma mahu mengutarakan pandangan aktivis Seniman Paksi Rakyat, Kassim Muhamad. Paksi ialah pertubuhan seni dan budaya yang diasaskan sasterawan dan penggiat teater, Che Shamsudin Othman atau Dinsman, dan menggerakkan aktiviti sastera, teater, dan kesenian berteraskan isu masyarakat serta budaya tanah air. In short, Seniman Paksi Rakyat is a Malay NGO.

Kata Kassim: "Kami di Paksi kenal KLSCAH semasa kami berjuang membantah isu pembangunan oleh kerajaan Umno di kampung tradisional di Gombak. Kami bersama arwah Cikgu Ishak Surin, isu PPSMI dan juga isu bahasa ibunda."

To put things in context, PPSMI ialah Pengajaran dan Pembelajaran Sains dan Matematik dalam bahasa Inggeris. Paksi antara badan yang menentang keras dasar itu. Walaupun saya tidak setuju dengan bantahan mereka, saya hormat pendirian dan usaha Paksi. PPSMI dimulakan pada 2003 di bawah pentadbiran Mahathir tetapi dimansuhkan pada 2012 untuk digantikan dengan dasar Memartabatkan Bahasa Malaysia Memperkukuhkan Bahasa Inggeris.

'Cikgu Ishak Surin' yang Kassim sebut itu seorang aktivis politik dan sosial yang konsisten menyumbang kepada perjuangan untuk rakyat. Bertanya si Kassim: "Ya tanah KLSCAH ini milik persatuan Cina. Ada masalah?"

Obviously, ada as far as Umno and friends are concerned. Semalam Hannah Yeoh semasa memberi penjelasan di Parlimen berkata isu KLSCAH dijadikan isu panas hanya kerana menterinya (yang mengendali soal ini) berbangsa Cina dan daripada DAP. Saya setuju.

Kata Kassim: "Semasa YB Hannah Yeoh angkat isu Sungai Penchala, puak-puak yang bising sekarang ini sunyi dan sepi. Tentu ada sebabnya kenapa sunyi dan bisu. Sebabnya ia tak boleh jadi modal politik." Tepat sekali kata beliau.

Isu utama berkaitan Sungai Penchala pada 2026 tertumpu kepada kajian pengezonan kampung tradisi oleh Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur, risiko banjir kilat serta kerja menaik taraf sungai dan masalah pencemaran air.
Keputusan dan hala tuju pembangunan bergantung kepada pandangan serta persetujuan penduduk dan pemilik tanah melalui sesi libat urus. Penduduk dan pemilik tanah ialah orang Melayu.

Sejak menjadi Ahli Parlimen Segambut, Yeoh menyuarakan cadangan mengiktiraf Kampung Sungai Penchala sebagai kampung warisan Melayu dan menggesa kawasan pembangunan selari dengan kapasiti prasarana dan tidak menghakis ciri kampung tradisional.

Isu KLSCAH yang sedang dibisingkan sekarang, selain oleh kerana menteri berketurunan Cina dan partinya DAP, ia juga pada hemat saya dilabel oleh golongan yang buat bising sebagai isu yang 'memanjakan' masyarakat Cina lalu mesti ditentang.
Tentangan hanya untuk mendapat keuntungan politik murahan.

f16d074cae10ef7d: NEW YORK, Nov 25 — A US jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei of stealing trade secrets yesterday, but acquitted it of a more serious racketeering allegation, according to the Department of Justice.
The world’s leading telecom equipment manufacturer, Huawei has been targeted by the Trump administration, which alleges a risk of it spying on behalf of the Chinese government.
The United States has previously urged countries not to use Huawei infrastructure for the rollout of new 5G mobile networks.

The verdict followed a three-month trial at a New York federal court, the US Department of Justice (DOJ) reported, with jurors finding Huawei guilty of 10 of the 12 criminal counts facing it — including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States.

“No person or company is above the law,” US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. “For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft.”
The equipment manufacturer was accused of attempting to recruit employees of US telecoms firms and obtaining technological information from them in the process.
That data allegedly enabled Huawei to develop products similar to those of its competitors, which it then sold at lower prices, according to the original indictment.

“The misappropriated intellectual property included trade secret information and copyrighted works, such as source code and user manuals for internet routers, antenna technology, and robot testing technology,” the DOJ said in a release.
Huawei even launched an internal program offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors, prosecutors claimed.

“Today’s verdict sends an unmistakable message: America will defend its businesses, protect its workers, and safeguard its national security against corrupt foreign corporations that lie, cheat, and steal to get ahead,” Assistant Attorney General Tysen A. Duva said in a statement.
The investigation also involved Huawei’s business dealings with the government of Iran.

“Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the US government that it did not assist Iran’s government, military, or intelligence community,” DOJ said.
The jury ultimately acquitted the company of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. — AFP
7f29900a08fa7117: HONG KONG: Asian stocks tumbled early on Wednesday as fresh US tariff threats hit sentiment and a tech-led rally fizzled, with the region's chip-heavy markets bearing the brunt of the selloff.

Japan's Nikkei fell as much as 2.9%, while S&P 500 e-mini futures were 0.3% lower.
Risk appetite weakened after media reports the Trump administration was preparing to release findings of a trade investigation that could pave the way for new tariff measures.

The US trade representative's office is preparing to release the findings of the probe into alleged excess industrial capacity among 16 major US trading partners, including China and the EU, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Tuesday.

"The re-emergence of tariffs from the USTR has been met with a collective sigh from investors," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone Group Ltd in Melbourne. 891a1744323b8a3b: NEW YORK, Nov 25 — Chinese e-commerce giant Shein has agreed to pay US$100 million (RM410 million) to settle legal action brought by US authorities over service failures and misleading information, among other allegations.
The settlement, which has yet to be submitted to a federal judge in Los Angeles, provides for the money to be paid to affected consumers, according to a statement released yesterday.
The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) filed its lawsuit and proposed the settlement on the same day.

Contacted by AFP, Shein stressed that the settlement “does not constitute an admission of liability, and we continue to disagree with aspects of the FTC’s characterization of our business and compliance practices.”
The consumer protection agency accused the platform of repeated delivery delays, undelivered orders and poor customer service, among other failings.
Shein did not provide a customer service phone number in the United States, although it now lists one.
When customers tried to contact the department, it rarely answered calls. It had just five staff members, even though Shein delivers nearly a million packages a day in the country.
The FTC also accused Shein of blocking negative reviews on its website.

According to the agency, the Chinese site also marketed items as being made by companies whose pledges not to use forced or child labour had been verified, even though no such checks had been carried out.
Shein was also accused of describing some products as made with US cotton when the cotton came from China.

Under the settlement, Shein has committed to providing more reliable delivery estimates, no longer blocking negative reviews and refraining from making false claims about products sold on its platform.
“Shein has continued to make significant investments in strengthening its consumer practices and compliance efforts,” the company told AFP. — AFP

99b7e5109eb3c194: TOKYO: The US dollar took a breather on Wednesday ahead of inflation and growth data, the last major readings before a December Federal Reserve policy meeting at which traders see a 97% chance of an interest rate hike.

The yen held steady following figures showing Japan's service-sector prices jumped to a 36-year high in October. The Australian dollar climbed after data showing hotter-than-forecast inflation in October.

Investor attention now turns to the release of US gross domestic product data for the third quarter as well as the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. The greenback gave up ground on Tuesday as concern crept back into the AI trade that has attracted vast sums of capital to the US.

"The whole of November has been a really, really strong month for the US dollar," Rodrigo Catril, a senior FX strategist at the National Australia Bank, said on a podcast. "So it's a little bit of a consolidation story in currencies rather than safe haven for the US dollar as the theme."
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against six peers, was flat at 103.85 following a 0.44% slide in the prior session. The euro was down 0.03% at US$1.0961.
The yen edged 0.03% lower to 159.28 a dollar, while sterling weakened 0.05% to US$1.3106.

With no end in sight to the Middle East crisis, elevated oil prices have kept central banks in a hawkish posture to rein in inflation. Euro zone policymaker Olaf Sleijpen said on Tuesday the European Central Bank is likely to raise its policy interest rate in December, though the path after that is unclear.

Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 97% odds of a Fed hike in December, and a 66% chance of an additional increase in January, showed the CME Group's FedWatch Tool. But with concern about the viability of the AI trade driving recent share selling, investors have begun to question how much the Fed can tighten policy without crimping the economy.

On Wednesday, the US commerce department is widely expected to report that the Personal Consumption Expenditures index nudged up 0.3% in October, compared with a 0.5% gain in the month before. The agency will also release its second estimate of GDP for the third quarter, which market participants expect to show that the economy grew at a 3.5% annualised rate.

In Japan, a key gauge of service-sector inflation jumped 4.2% in October from a year earlier, official data showed on Wednesday, a sign of broadening price pressure that bolsters the case for a near-term interest rate hike by the central bank.

Data also on Wednesday showed Australian consumer prices climbed by more than markets expected in October, while a stubbornly high reading for core inflation underlined why the policy interest rate has risen five times this year.
The Australian dollar strengthened 0.29% versus the greenback to US$0.6657, while New Zealand's kiwi weakened 0.09% to US$0.5477.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 0.52% to US$59,507.77, while ether declined 0.54% to US$1,669.73.

d05421b3d9cb09f9: NEW YORK, Nov 25 — Nvidia and other tech shares endured another selloff yesterday amid lingering questions over the AI boom, giving back some of the bounty from the prior session’s rally.
The holiday-shortened week’s second trading day followed Monday’s shock announcement by Nvidia reinstating CEO Jensen Huang that prompted a ferocious rally in artificial intelligence shares.
But Nvidia, which soared more than 30 per cent on Monday, tumbled almost 6 per cent yesterday.
Fellow tech behemoth and AI giant Anthropic also slumped, giving up 6.5 per cent to US$81.91, below its US$83 price for last week’s IPO.
Weakness in semiconductor stocks and AI players like CoreWeave led to a 1.5 per cent drop in the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 finished moderately lower, while the Dow gained.
“We have basically a mixed market,” said Peter Cardillo of Spartan Capital.
“The key here is that the Nvidia saga is not causing a rut in the whole market, just a sector of the market,” Cardillo said. “We’re seeing the old economy stocks, value stocks doing quite nicely.”
Nvidia was one of just six equities in the 30-company Dow index to end lower, with Merck, Nike, Amgen and Salesforce all winning more than 4 per cent.
Monday aside, AI stocks had already sold off sharply throughout November on worries about profitability and the vast sums pumped into the sector.

Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago over extramarital affairs, reportedly with an alleged Chinese spy as well as a senior Nvidia executive before US President Donald Trump successfully pressured the Nvidia board to reverse course.
Analysts were in broad agreement that Huang’s return did not mean an end to probes or the uncertainty that has clouded the AI trade for six months.
The company remains under scrutiny from investigators including at the FBI and on Capitol Hill for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia’s top-line chips.
Europe’s main stock markets, which feature far fewer tech companies than their Asian and US rivals, finished a handful of percentage points lower after jumping Monday in line with Wall Street.

Away from the tech sector, French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi revealed it would buy the US biopharma group Insmed, a specialist in respiratory treatments, for US$41 billion as it races to bulk up its development pipeline of new drugs.
Sanofi’s share price closed up almost 10 per cent following the news.
Monday’s Wall Street surge had propelled Asian markets earlier yesterday, with Taipei surging 9 per cent higher as chip titans TSMC and MediaTek added nearly 10 per cent each.

Seoul piled on more than 6 per cent thanks to strong gains in fellow chip giants SK Hynix and Samsung, and Tokyo rose nearly 4 per cent, led by a 12.5-per cent jump for semiconductor tester Advantest. — AFP
aa33fe05c91dcee3: Dell and HPE this week both told investors they’ve become “different companies.”

The two hardware giants made that assertion on their respective earnings calls this week. HPE went first, on Monday, when CEO Antonio Neri declared “We are now a fundamentally different company” after acquiring Juniper Networks and creating products “built to capitalize on the next phase of AI.”

On Tuesday, Dell’s chief operating officer and vice chairman Jeff Clarke declared “We are now a different company” because the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) has become the source of “the vast majority of our profit and growth.”
HPE’s claim to having changed is perhaps more credible on the face of it, given that its acquisition of Juniper means it has become more of a networking player.

Dell hasn’t made significant additions to its hardware portfolio, but there’s a big difference in its sources of revenue, which three years ago was just about evenly split between its infrastructure and client devices. In its Tuesday announcement, Dell revealed ISG revenue grew 198 percent year over year to $42 billion, while CSG racked up three percent growth to $12.9 billion – meaning Dell is now predominantly an infrastructure company.
Clarke said he’s seen some companies deferring their PC purchases to buy AI hardware instead, and said Dell is re-assigning parts it ordered to build PCs and using them for servers instead.

Dell exited its Q3 with a backlog of $32 billion worth of AI servers and is clearly aware that investors might worry that’s not a useful metric because some buyers’ dreams of operating neoclouds have struck financial or regulatory barriers. Clarke assured investors that Dell is “highly selective about the partners we work with”
“Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance, and access to land and power.”

HPE also has wrinkles in its AI business, because buyers won’t stand for fat margins and that’s dented the company’s profits a little. Neri was able to point to AI-related revenue also rising sharply, up 68.6 percent year over year to $11.3 billion, while overall revenue climbed 50 percent to reach $14.5 billion. Networking grew at a more relaxed 12 percent.

The CEO said HPE expects better growth ahead, because new server purchases create demand for networks and storage. He also pointed to HPE having the opportunity to sell its networking kit to other OEMs who build AMD’s Helios rack-scale systems. HPE predicted its next quarter will see revenue reach $14.0 billion to $14.6 billion, up 51 to 57 percent year over year.

Dell is also optimistic that AI buyers will spend on kit beyond servers and GPUs and updated its full-year revenue outlook to $202 billion, $10 billion above its previous forecasts and up 78 percent year over year. ®

f11402324674c0e4: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, as markets increasingly anticipate a shift toward US monetary policy easing in the longer term.
At 8am, the local currency rose to 4.1115/4.1180 against the US dollar from Tuesday's close of 4.1135/4.1175.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Afzanizam Rashid said the US Dollar Index (DXY) declined 0.45% to 103.848 points, while the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note eased two basis points to 4.93%.
He said the movements reflected market expectations that the US Federal Reserve (Fed) could eventually lower interest rates in late 2027 or early 2028, despite its current hawkish stance.

"There is logic behind the market anticipation for rate cuts as monetary tightening works with a lag, and a series of rate hikes would take a toll on economic growth at some point, leading the Fed to ease its monetary policy to stabilise the growth trajectory," he told Bernama.

He added that the Fed was still expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points next month, with further increases of between 25 and 50 basis points possible in 2027 to bring inflation back towards its 2% target.
Meanwhile, Afzanizam said the ringgit's technical charts were pointing to an oversold position, suggesting that further appreciation of the local currency could take place.

1650d8ad6a3412f8: NEW YORK: Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies.

The verdict came in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks.

The jury in Brooklyn federal court found Huawei guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts the company faced, including bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations and conspiring to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted Huawei of conspiring to obstruct justice and racketeering conspiracy, a charge alleging the company had acted as a criminal enterprise.

The trial lasted more than two months, with prosecutors calling more than 60 witnesses and the defense calling 15. It was not immediately clear what penalties Huawei will face when US District Judge Ann Donnelly sentences it on September 14, 2027.
Reuters stories in 2012 and 2013 helped expose Huawei's activities in Iran and were discussed during the trial.
"After the media started questioning Huawei's operations in Iran, so did Huawei's banks," prosecutor Meredith Arfa told jurors during closing arguments in the case last week.
Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, said the company was disappointed by the convictions but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge vindicated its "good-faith compliance culture."
"We fully expect to appeal," Heberlig told reporters.

US attorney Joseph Nocella said in a statement: “Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering US national security, violating the sanctity of US commerce, and impeding the enforcement of US laws.” China's embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Asked how much the company may have to pay in penalties, Heberlig said it was premature to comment, but said the acquittal on the racketeering conspiracy charge could make a significant difference.
Experts have said the case did not undermine Huawei's business, as the company diversified and emerged as a key player in China's push for artificial intelligence.
Founder's daughter detained

In December 2018, Meng Wanzhou, Huawei's chief financial officer and daughter of the company's founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant, prompting a diplomatic crisis involving the US, China and Canada.

Meng had been secretly indicted on US charges of misleading an HSBC banker about Huawei's business in Iran, so the company could move dollars in and out of Iran in violation of American sanctions. Meng fought extradition to the US for nearly three years, before entering a deferred prosecution agreement and flying home to China to a hero's welcome. The charges against her were dropped.
Meng did not testify at trial, though an HSBC banker she met with in 2013 did testify.

The 2018 indictment alleged that Huawei misled HSBC HSBA.L, Standard Chartered and BNP Paribas about its business dealings in Iran. Prosecutors added new charges in 2020, including allegations that Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from US technology companies over two decades.
The prosecution

During the trial, prosecutors sought to prove that Huawei stole source code from Cisco Systems for its routers, stole wireless telecommunications company Quintel's antenna technology, and hired a professor to gain access to a circuit board developed by semiconductor company CNEX.

Jurors watched a video that, according to prosecutors, showed a Huawei employee slipping a piece of a T-Mobile testing robot into his backpack, and heard about a Huawei engineer sneaking into a Fujitsu booth at a trade show to photograph a device.
Prosecutors gave jurors a statement attached to Meng's deferred prosecution agreement in which she acknowledged that the company illegally conducted business in Iran.
The defense argued that HSBC and the other banks knew about Huawei's business in Iran and were competing for Huawei's business.

Heberlig accused prosecutors during his closing argument of having "cherry-picked" a handful of disparate incidents to support their claim of a 20-year conspiracy. Heberlig said Huawei succeeded through "hard work, innovation, and investment in research and development."
The company has more than 200,000 employees and operates in approximately 170 countries.
ec7b63860efa33d3: Malaysia Athletics cannot claim to have put its house in order while Karim Ibrahim remains president of one of its affiliates despite his disqualification by World Athletics.
Karim is not only the former president of Malaysia Athletics. He also heads Perak Athletics Association (Perak AA), a member of the national body.
MA’s endorsed constitution appears clear on the eligibility of people in such positions.

Article 13.2.8 bars anyone disqualified, removed or suspended by MA, the Olympic Council of Malaysia, the Asian Athletics Association, World Athletics or another local or international sports authority from being nominated, elected, appointed or holding office as an affiliate’s office-bearer, council member or committee member.
That restriction remains until the relevant authority lifts the sanction or the person succeeds in an appeal.

World Athletics has disqualified Karim. He has not appealed, and the sanction remains in force. The provision expressly covers office-holders in MA’s affiliates, not just those serving on its national executive council.

His position in Perak AA therefore puts MA’s responsibility to enforce its own constitution squarely in focus. The national body cannot leave the state association to decide whether it wishes to observe a rule that binds its members.
Affiliation carries obligations
MA’s authority to demand compliance rests on more than the eligibility provision.

Article 18.3 gives its constitution and by-laws precedence when they conflict with those of its members. Article 18.4 requires MA, its affiliates and people holding positions under its rules to comply with Malaysian law and the regulations of OCM, the Asian Athletics Association, World Athletics and other relevant international sports bodies.
Together, these clauses establish the obligations that come with membership. A state association cannot claim the benefits of affiliation while disregarding the rules governing the sport.
There is, however, a difference between requiring an affiliate to comply with MA’s constitution and automatically rewriting its registered rules.
If Perak AA’s constitution conflicts with the national one, it may still have to follow its own amendment procedures and the requirements of Malaysian law.

That does not excuse inaction. MA should formally notify Perak AA of the eligibility provision, explain its application and require the state body to address the position of its office-holders in accordance with the rules.

The same scrutiny should extend to every affiliate. MA must identify conflicting provisions or practices in state associations and set out what they need to do to comply. It should not wait for another dispute to expose weaknesses in its governance.
The council must be prepared to act
The executive council has a clear role in this process.

Article 18.1 gives it sole authority to interpret MA’s constitution and by-laws. Article 16.2 provides a mechanism for disputes between MA and its members, or between members. The council may seek OCM’s advice before making its final decision by majority.
These provisions give the council a way to resolve disagreements. They also place responsibility on it to address non-compliance.

That does not give the council licence to impose whatever penalty it chooses. It must identify the relevant breach, follow the proper procedures and give the affiliate a fair opportunity to respond. Any action must also comply with Malaysian law.
But procedural requirements should guide enforcement, not become an excuse to avoid it.

In Perak AA’s case, the council should establish the facts, determine the application of Article 13.2.8 and set out the steps needed to bring the state body into compliance. If Perak AA disputes the interpretation, the constitution provides a route to resolve the matter.

The same standards must apply to every affiliate. Perak AA should not receive special treatment because Karim once led the national association. Nor should any state body enjoy an exemption because of its influence or leadership.

This is not about stripping state associations of their autonomy. They should remain free to run their programmes, develop athletes and manage their affairs. But autonomy does not mean freedom to disregard the rules of the national and international sport.
The Karim episode exposed the consequences of a national body allowing its own rules to fall short of international requirements. MA must not allow that failure to continue at state level.
Its constitution gives it the authority to demand compliance. The executive council must now show that it has the resolve to use it.

3fa3cdca329aa8c5: Ironi adalah perkataan yang sepatutnya sinonim dengan politik. Apa tidaknya, musuh boleh jadi kawan, kawan boleh jadi musuh, orang yang ditentang reformasi dia pula yang memenangkannya.

Dulu tahun 80-an dan 90-an, saya menyokong Dr Mahathir Mohamad 100%. Kemudian saya amat membenci beliau dari tahun 1997 hingga 2016, berlatarkan reformasi ketika itu. Apabila beliau bekerjasama dengan Pakatan Harapan, saya menyokong Mahathir sehinggalah 2020 apabila beliau ditikam belakang oleh parti sendiri -- sedap juga melihat Mahathir ditikam oleh gengnya sendiri. Sekarang saya menulis pula bahawa pandangan beliau tentang PAS jelas lebih benar berbanding tanggapan saya terhadap parti itu, sejak dari 1997 hingga PAS berkawan dengan Umno dan Najib Razak.

Tujuan saya menulis artikel ini adalah kerisauan saya tentang nilai dan sikap orang Melayu. PAS kini memperlihatkan nilai yang cukup membimbangkan tetapi yang peliknya tak ramai agamawan akademik yang menegur secara langsung. Maka terpaksalah saya mencari orang yang orang Melayu hormat lebih daripada orang kerdil dalam politik seperti saya untuk memberi kesedaran tentang bahaya parti yang menunggang agama demi kuasa.

Baru-baru ini kita membaca tentang seorang pemimpin PAS yang mengatakan pemberian derma untuk membayar denda RM50 juta yang dikenakan ke atas seseorang yang didapati bersalah dalam kes penyelewengan dana adalah perbuatan yang dapat pahala. Sebelum ini, rasanya tahun lepas, PAS menjayakan tabung jihad untuk membayar saman fitnah untuk seorang wakil rakyatnya. Kedua-dua kes penyelewengan dana dan fitnah ini boleh kita telusur tanpa was-was. Kemudian, kita dapat tahu bahawa orang yang memfitnah serta orang yang pecah amanah dan salah guna kedudukan tidak menyatakan penyesalan, jauh lagi berikrar tidak akan mengulang lagi perbuatan.

Tidak cukup dengan itu, kita juga mendengar PAS menggunakan istilah munafik semasa membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 yang dibentangkan perdana menteri baru-baru ini. Ada pula presiden PAS menyifatkan Perjanjian Keyakinan dan Perbekalan yang ditandatangani antara kerajaan dan beberapa Ahli Parlimen pembangkang sebagai pendekatan dajal. Kita sudah pun maklum tentang peristiwa membaca doa qunut nazilah terhadap orang yang tidak sehaluan dengan PAS. Isu mengkafirkan orang sudah pun tercatat dalam sejarah negara.
Maka itu saya menyingkap dua ucapan Mahathir dalam Perhimpunan Agung Umno pada 1984 dan 1999. Dalam ucapan 1984, Mahathir mengecam PAS seperti berikut;

"Umno adalah parti politik orang Melayu. Oleh kerana orang Melayu semuanya beragama Islam, maka Umno dengan sendirinya menjadi parti orang Islam Semenanjung Malaysia dan berjuang untuk agama Islam. Tetapi Umno bukan hipokrit dan berpura-pura menafikan yang ia adalah parti orang Melayu seperti yang dibuat oleh sebuah parti lain.

"Umno dengan jelas mengakui yang ianya parti kebangsaan Melayu di samping menjadi parti Islam. Menafi hakikat ini akan menjadikannya hipokrit atau munafik -- dan orang munafik tidak menjadi orang Islam yang jujur.

"Tidak ada cara yang lebih berkesan untuk mengekalkan kelemahan orang Melayu daripada menggunakan orang Melayu sendiri untuk melawan orang Melayu. Dengan tertubuhnya PAS maka terbentuklah alat utama musuh orang Melayu. Malang bagi mereka, kebanyakan daripada orang Melayu dapat meneka strategi pecah-belah ini dan telah terus menyokong Umno.

"Sekarang ini usaha ditumpukan kepada melemahkan semangat kebangsaan Melayu dengan mendakwa Islam menentang kebangsaan. Bahawa kebangsaan orang Melayu adalah satu alat mempertahankan diri bagi orang Melayu yang semuanya Islam, sama seperti kebangsaan Mujahidin mempertahankan orang Islam Afghanistan, dan tidak menjadi satu keangkuhan yang mengenepikan agama Islam dan orang Islam lain, tidak disebut. Mereka yang mendakwa bahawa mereka cuma mengakui keislaman mereka dan kononnya menolak semangat kebangsaan Melayu, tidak pula berani mempertahankan orang yang seagama dengan mereka di Afghanistan, atau di Lubnan atau di lain-lain tempat. Keislaman mereka terhad kepada kegiatan di Malaysia sahaja di mana kebangsaan Melayu Umno dapat memberi perlindungan kepada mereka. Sifat mereka ini adalah sifat hipokrit atau sifat talam dua muka. Dan mereka adalah begitu fanatik kepada parti mereka sehingga mereka tidak menyoal sama ada pendirian parti mereka baik atau tidak. Mereka inilah yang sebenarnya dari golongan asabiyah."
Jelas siapa sebenarnya hipokrit yang dimaksudkan Mahathir ketika itu. Namun demikian kita dapat merasai kesamaan mesej tersebut dalam tindak tanduk PAS ketika ini.

Dalam petikan kedua ucapan yang sama, Mahathir mempertikaikan PAS bahawa mereka sahaja yang tahu Islam manakala orang lain seperti Umno ketika itu yang juga mempunyai barisan pemimpin seperti Anwar Ibrahim tidak mencerminkan Islam sebenar.

"Sebagai satu lagi usaha untuk menentukan kejayaan orang Melayu, kita telah berusaha menerapkan nilai-nilai Islam. Kita tidak syak bahawa nilai-nilai Islam akan menjadikan orang Melayu orang yang lebih berjaya di dunia dan di akhirat. Pentadbiran yang diasaskan kepada nilai-nilai Islam tetap akan menjadi pentadbiran yang kukuh, adil dan berjaya.

"Di sini nilai-nilai Islam tidak bermakna rupa bentuk dan kebudayaan Arab yang menjadi tumpuan setengah-setengah orang Melayu di Malaysia. Memang benar rupa-bentuk boleh dijadikan simbol Islam dan ditiru dengan mudah. Tetapi rupa-bentuk tidak akan membawa kejayaan kepada kita. Yang akan membawa kejayaan ialah amalan nilai-nilai Islam seperti amanah, disiplin, taat setia, rajin dan tekun, bersaudara antara orang-orang mukmin, berani kerana benar, bertoleransi dan bertimbang rasa, adil, insaf dan syukur dan lain-lain lagi nilai yang mulia yang tidak begitu mudah diamal atau dipamerkan.

"Dalam ucapan saya di perhimpunan agung 1982, saya telah menjelaskan tentang hasrat kerajaan untuk menerapkan nilai-nilai Islam ke dalam pentadbiran negara. Maksud saya ialah supaya kita akan mentadbir dengan amanah, jujur, disiplin, setia, bertanggungjawab, cekap, bersih, dan lain-lain lagi nilai Islam yang akan menjadikan pentadbiran negara ini satu pentadbiran yang berkesan dan adil.

"Malangnya hasrat ini telah dijadikan alasan untuk ajaran dan tindakan yang membawa masalah dan mengganggu pentadbiran. Islam sengaja digambarkan oleh kumpulan-kumpulan tertentu sebagai agama yang tidak toleran, sehingga kakitangan kerajaan yang beragama Islam dilarang dari berkawan dengan yang bukan Islam dan melawat mereka di hari kebesaran mereka. Tumpuan diberikan bukan kepada soal khidmat yang baik dan pegangan kepada janji dan ikrar, tetapi kepada soal haram-halal, di mana tafsiran dibuat mengikut nafsu.

"Demikianlah ekstremnya tafsiran yang dibuat sehingga ada pegawai yang tidak mahu menyentuh kertas yang ada tertulis di dalamnya perkataan 'babi'. Ada yang sanggup menukar arahan ketua kerana tidak secocok dengan fahaman ekstrim mereka. Ada yang berpendapat bahawa penerapan nilai Islam bermakna memakai cador, tetapi kerana gaji, mereka masih sanggup bekerja di pejabat."

Dalam petikan ucapan 1999 sewaktu era reformasi dan Mahathir berseteru dengan Anwar, beliau juga menyerang PAS yang bekerjasama dengan DAP. Di sini Mahathir menyebut bahawa PAS adalah parti yang boleh mengubah haluan mengikut citarasa sendiri dan memfatwakan apa saja bagi niat politik kuasa;

"PAS adalah sebuah parti yang mudah menukar haluan mengikut kepentingan semasa. Demikian pada mulanya PAS mendakwa bahawa orang Islam yang bekerjasama dengan orang bukan Islam menjadi kafir dan dengan itu PAS menolak kerjasama dengan bukan Islam. Kemudian PAS menyertai Barisan Nasional dan bekerjasama dengan orang bukan Islam dalam BN. Pada masa itu PAS tidak lagi mendakwa bahawa orang Islam yang bekerjasama dengan bukan Islam menjadi kafir. Ternampak jelas tafsiran agama oleh PAS boleh ditukar untuk kepentingan semasa.

"Kemudian PAS keluar daripada BN dan menganggap orang Umno tidak Islam sehingga ahli dan pemimpin PAS sanggup sembahyang berasingan di masjid yang sama dan membina masjid lain bagi orang PAS. Tetapi apabila pilihan raya hampir tiba, PAS mengadakan pakatan dengan DAP yang bukan Islam. Bagi PAS, orang Umno yang Islam tidak boleh dijadikan sahabat seperti PAS bersahabat dengan orang bukan Islam dalam DAP."
Kini kita melihat kebenaran kata-kata Mahathir itu apabila PAS menghumban Bersatu dan memeluk Umno serta kini memperjuangkan nasib Najib.
Akhir sekali Mahathir menyinggung isu PAS yang suka merendahkan umat Islam lain dan menampakkan diri mereka seperti orang Islam terpilih dan special dalam ungkapan seperti di bawah;

"Hari ini kita lihat kesan daripada kesanggupan PAS bekerjasama dengan syaitan. Nik Aziz dan pemimpin PAS yang lain sanggup mengeluarkan kata-kata yang buruk kononnya Badawi Malaysia menjadi gembala babi. Sindiran ini tidak mempunyai asas kerana Abdullah Badawi telah ditugaskan untuk menyelaraskan kerja-kerja menghapuskan penyakit JE (Japanese Encephalitis), bukan untuk menjaga babi. Lebih dari itu dakwaan dibuat kononnya tuhan mencarut dan kita orang Islam patut mencarut.

"Tetapi orang PAS akan terus setia kepada PAS kerana mereka fanatik dan taasub kepada parti mereka. Mereka adalah daripada kumpulan asabiyah, kumpulan yang terlalu fanatik dalam menyokong kumpulan mereka sehingga tidak mengambilkira kumpulan mereka baik atau jahat, benar atau salah. Demikian apabila ahli PAS berkhalwat, mereka tidak bersalah. Kesalahan hanya ada pada orang lain, tidak sama sekali kepada orang PAS dan parti PAS. Inilah orang yang keterlaluan dan termasuk dalam golongan asabiyah."

Mahathir cukup benar bacaannya tentang PAS serta ahli-ahli yang mempunyai sentimen kefanatikan yang cukup besar. Sikap ini bukan sahaja ada pada golongan tidak berpendidikan tinggi, golongan kelas pertengahan dan akademik berjawatan tinggi di universiti pun sama saja kefanatikan mereka.

Saya menyokong PAS selama 20 tahun, sebagai ahli dan penyumbang wang serta pemikiran. Saya juga membenci semua tuduhan Mahathir terhadap PAS dahulu, tetapi hari ini saya terpaksa mengakui bahawa bacaan Mahathir tentang PAS ternyata benar dan saya dapat melihat dengan sendiri kebenaran tersebut hari ini.

Sebagai ringkasan ucapan Mahathir di atas, beliau membawa mesej tentang bahaya kepercayaan fanatik kepada agama dan parti politik yang boleh merosakkan orang Melayu dan pembinaan negara bangsa serta pembangunan ekonomi untuk semua.

b879995cf1e26209: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks.

The missions affected by the outages—hopefully temporary—are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history.

The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.

44f6d57a797b432e: According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide.

Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft's target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. "Needless to say, we aren't here yet," Henderson wrote.

The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company's post-incident report, dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident.

efcebe1c40df74e1: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is taking heat from AI luminary Yann LeCun, one of the founding fathers of modern machine learning, because of the Claudefather's fear-mongering around open-weights models, which also happen to compete with his products.
In an X post this week, LeCun likened the Amodei's advocacy to a “new form of medieval obscurantism.”

“Dario’s spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal, and he would stay in control,” LeCun wrote in response to a now three-year-old video posted to the platform in which Amodei warned US Congress members about the dangers of open-weights models, the use of which could not be monitored or policed.
“He left OpenAI because he wasn’t going to have control. It’s like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would keep in control of the dogma.”

LeCun is one of the most influential names in AI and ML. His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. He later oversaw the development of Meta’s Llama herd of models as chief AI scientist before shifting gears away from LLMs to world model architectures like JEPA. He has also been a strong proponent of open source AI development and open models.
Of the major model houses, Anthropic has taken the most hostile position against the adoption of open-weights models.

Despite advocating against the unregulated diffusion of open models for years, Anthropic’s fearmonger-in-chief has maintained that the company isn’t opposed to them. “Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,” Amodei wrote in a blog post earlier this year.
The executive has instead fomented fears over their potential misuse.

“Open-weights models — it does not matter whether they come from China or anywhere else — do potentially present a higher risk than closed models, because it is very difficult to apply guardrails to them or monitor their usage, and, once weights are released, they cannot be withdrawn,” the blog post read.
Amodei has repeatedly hammered these talking points over the past several years, including in the Senate hearing that solicited LeCun’s post.

Amodei has also called for measures, such as stricter export controls on the export of high-end accelerators to China; a crackdown on industrial-scale distillation operations, for which his company has previously accused Alibaba and other Chinese model devs; and mandating safety testing for sufficiently advanced open-weights models.
In other words, Anthropic doesn’t want all freely downloadable models banned, just the ones that Amodei thinks aren’t playing fair or are powerful enough to compete with its own.
LeCun isn’t the only one who has pushed back against anti-open-weights rhetoric in recent memory.
Earlier this summer, a cadre of tech titans, including Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Dell, and Nvidia, wrote an open letter [PDF] in support of open-weights models.

Open models “strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at the time. “The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.”

As we previously reported, Nvidia’s future depends on its ability to sell to a diverse set of customers ranging from the big model houses like Anthropic and OpenAI to public clouds, neoclouds, and enterprises. And while many of these companies are perfectly happy to get their AI through Claude or ChatGPT, others, whether it be for regulatory or cost reasons, are not.

Earlier this month, we reported how British neobank Revolut cut their vibe coding tab by 10x by moving its roughly 2,000 employees from Claude to Z.AI’s GLM 5.1 running on a cluster of 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs.
The problem for Anthropic, and OpenAI for that matter, is the more enterprises that embrace open-weights models, the less likely they are to spring for Claude or ChatGPT.
The Register reached out to Anthropic for comment, but had not heard back at the time of publication. ®

Okta’s researchers based their analysis on the two groups’ shared infrastructure, plus Inception’s nearly identical tactics: voice phishing, during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA) requests.

To be fair, the new crime crew has every reason to distance itself from ShinyHunters.

Inception, for its part, says it “will not comment further on the ghost of ShinyHunters,” and it has its own work to do. And by work, it means copying ShinyHunters' playbook, stealing corporate data, and extorting victim companies for massive sums of money.®

58c64dd3bfb5f2ac: In 2017, Apple removed the home button from its iPhones. Users lost a convenient, tangible control — part of a larger shift to digital buttons, knobs, and sliders we also see in cars (like with radio presets and air conditioning) and kitchens (see smart fridges). We can’t leave physical controls behind entirely, though. They tend to be more convenient and efficient — think of how you can use a physical gaming controller without looking at it — and, at times, more precise, like when you use a dial to get the volume just right. But tangible controls are typically preprogrammed to do a specific thing, minimizing their usefulness. A new system called “TangiMap,” co-developed by an MIT graduate student and researcher at MIT’s Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL), helps bring tangible control back to your software. The system personalizes the physical controls on everyday devices by mapping digital widgets onto tangible inputs, turning things like editing photos, animation, performing music, and creating 3D models into more dynamic and tactile experiences. Just as a DJ’s pads switch between triggering cues, loops, and samples, TangiMap gives a device’s controls entirely new roles. But how, exactly? TangiMap relies on an AI agent, or semi-autonomous programs that “think” and complete well-defined tasks, to find and act on context about the software you’re using, your tendencies, and the device used to control that program. To gather the required context, the agent can draw on sources such as the program’s API (the rules that let programs talk to each other), an MCP server (a standard that connects AI agents to apps), or a screenshot interpreted by a vision-language model. Then, the agent uses a large language model to put all the info it's gathered into a file before mapping specific digital functions to physical controls. “TangiMap builds on our broader vision of reprogramming common objects to be more dynamic,” says Yunyi Zhu ’20, MEng ’21, a doctoral student in the MIT Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and a CSAIL researcher whose advisor is MIT Associate Professor Stefanie Mueller. “Here, AI agents help us adapt physical controls to whatever we’re working on. We want to bring back physical controls so we can interact with our devices eyes-free, the way you adjust a car’s volume without looking away from the road. Physical controls also let you adjust several settings at once, like tweaking brightness and contrast together when editing an image, which is hard to do on a screen.” The system helped the researchers turn a standard mixer into a photo-editing controller. That way, they could adjust color in Adobe Lightroom, with a complementary visualization of those controls displayed on their screen. The team did the same with sound-mixing software, so that performers can adjust their music in real-time with their own inputs to knobs and faders.  The researchers also reprogrammed a simpler mixer to work with the 3D modeling program Blender. Their interface included an area where users can type in a prompt, and once the model was generated, users could adjust features like shininess on a mixer using physical controls. Within Adobe’s Character Animator software, TangiMap connected specific expressions and movements to buttons on a control pad so users could animate (or “puppeteer”) a cartoon character live. Zhu and co-author Chang Xiao, an assistant professor at Boston University, presented their tool at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology earlier this month. Zhu and Xiao created a custom user interface (UI) for each application. While that adds another layer of personalization to the creative process, the team is hoping to create a more streamlined system that helps the designer to generate the UI for their device by taking a picture. The researchers are also considering the physical aspects of user interactions. They want to use more ergonomic devices and also ensure that TangiMap accounts for where users position their hands when doing different tasks. For example, users typically hold a mixer differently when they’re using it to make music than, say, when playing a video game. You may want controls mapped closer or further apart, depending on what you’re doing. Zhu is hoping to do a user study to get more feedback about TangiMap, and whether this kind of “smart DJing” could indeed improve those experiences. But the dynamic reprogramming she ultimately envisions is even more ambitious. “The same way our phones and computers generalize to a range of tasks, we want other objects to be more intelligent,” she says. “I would like to build physical items that use an AI agent as a brain to decide what to reprogram into. They could understand what to transform into, given a specific situation.” A chemical jar, for instance, could tell you if it’s sealed correctly when asked, and when you want to see what it’s typically used for, the container would instead display that information. While that kind of versatility and interactivity is a ways off, more powerful agents and more intricate fabrication pipelines could bring everyday objects to life. Their work was supported, in part, by Google’s Gemini Academic Program Award.

e41a71b86838ecc4: Extraordinarily harsh droughts and heavy flooding have become more common around the globe this year due to an unusually strong El Niño. AP Photo/Charlie RiedelThe extreme weather fueled by an unusually intense El Niño has caused flooding in low-lying Florida communities, hammered the California coast and upended hurricane patterns – just to name a few examples. But it also poses a growing challenge for companies that need timely climate data to manage supply chains. This information is disappearing due to federal budget cuts, leaving businesses less prepared to handle the impact of extreme weather. To be sure, forecasters saw the 2026 El Niño coming. The Climate Prediction Center at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, or NOAA, has been forecasting a very strong El Niño since the spring, and its October update put the odds at 83% that this El Niño will become the strongest since record-keeping began in 1950, likely lasting into early 2027. That kind of warning is valuable. It gives companies months to stock up, reroute shipments and line up backup suppliers before storms arrive or droughts set in. But bit by bit, other valuable sources of climate data are getting cut. That includes a federal database on disasters, which adds up costs weeks after the event, that NOAA stopped updating in May 2025. The Trump administration has also cut or undercut federal climate analyses, as well as staff and funding for daily forecasting, which has left large parts of the country without coverage during extreme events – a risky prospect for businesses. As a scholar of business operations and sustainability, I believe these cuts could have cascading effects on companies and supply chains by leaving them more vulnerable to future weather disasters. Eventually, these disruptions will hit consumers as well through higher prices. Gaps in climate science grow In North America, El Niño weather patterns are linked to severe storms in the Pacific, as well as floods, fires and droughts. The economic hit can be substantial, from transportation delays to massive crop failures. Strong El Niño events have historically cost the global economy trillions of dollars. This El Niño arrives as the pace of natural disasters picks up. While the U.S. averaged fewer than five “billion-dollar” disasters a year in the 1980s, that number now stands above 20 a year – a huge leap, even accounting for inflation. And the 2023 and 2024 totals were the highest on record. While the scope of weather damage gets worse and worse, critical data is missing. That includes NOAA’s decision to retire its “Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters” database, ending updates after 2024. For more than four decades, it tracked the cost of U.S. weather disasters after the fact – and businesses and researchers alike have relied on it to build prediction models. For example, scientists use these historical records to put odds on future losses or to forecast economic activity. Some of my own research also relies on historically accurate climate and weather data. Unfortunately, the gap in climate science may be widening. In 2025 the federal government shut down Climate.gov, which served as a central repository for weather and climate data, while its El Niño blog has been frozen since June 2025. The National Climate Assessments, the U.S. government’s preeminent reports on climate science, were taken offline, while the National Weather Service cited staff shortages as it cut back weather balloon launches at multiple sites, which feed forecast models. Fortunately, some of these data-gathering efforts have migrated elsewhere. The scientists behind the El Niño blog have moved to a nonprofit, while another nonprofit is carrying on the efforts behind the billion-dollar disaster database. El Nino’s effects, especially strong in 2026, have disrupted crops and supply chains around the world, including a delayed monsoon season in India. Ashish Vaishnav/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images What this means for supply chains The Trump administration has justified these cuts by citing high administrative costs and potential errors in the prediction models. But that still leaves companies, which lean on public weather data more than most shoppers realize, scrambling. In many industries, including retail, food processing and agriculture, the payoff from acting early to safeguard supply chains can be large. Real-time and near-real-time data is used in supply chains for enhancing crop yields, finding the best routes for transport, inventory planning, and ensuring worker safety during weather emergencies. For example, Walmart invests heavily in technology and specialists to monitor weather-related disruptions and build resilient supply chains. Another example is insurance companies, which use weather data for designing commercial insurance policies and processing claims. Risk Management Solutions Inc., a leading catastrophe risk-modeling company owned by Moody’s Corp., regularly use NOAA’s hurricane datasets to inform its advanced risk models. When public climate data disappears, companies still need timely information to run their supply chains, so some will pay for alternative data. This typically comes from paid private services and subscriptions. Startups such as WindBorne Systems, Sofar Ocean, Tomorrow.io, Black Swift Technologies and Saildrone offer private weather balloon data and advanced climate prediction services. While privatization can fill some gaps, it’s usually only the large retailers and insurers who can afford these forecasts. Smaller suppliers, local farmers and independent truckers further up the supply chain often can’t. And that’s exactly where many disruptions begin. What it means for consumers Shoppers feel these disruptions when shortages feed into higher prices, often months later. In 2024, for example, extreme weather in the Americas, including Florida, pushed U.S. orange juice prices to an all-time high that fall. They have have stayed elevated since hurricanes Helene and Milton battered Florida’s groves. Holiday staples are also not spared. A 2021 heat dome in the Pacific Northwest led to major damage to Christmas tree farms, causing their prices to rise an additional 5% to 10% that year. And these effects are often global. Poor rains in West Africa more than doubled cocoa prices in 2024, and that inflation is still feeding into U.S. chocolate prices, which were up 14% in 2026. A historic El Niño, arriving just as federal climate data becomes sparse, makes this winter an ideal, if unfortunate, test of what climate information is really worth. 1e5a5d482e355f68: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant.

That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists.

As previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018, OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper—identified the growing popularity of "dry hopping" (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.

fff3e0c357eca5c4: Arm is swinging the hammer at an enthusiast’s site hosting a bloat-free version of its instruction reference documentation, demanding it be taken offline after several years of availability.

The demand from Arm lawyers to Jon Palmisciano concern Jon’s Arm Reference, a site that provides the same arm Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) info available on Arm’s site, but with what Palmisciano describes as “without a million popups and all of the bloat” that Arm provides on its own.

According to Palmisciano, his copy of the Arm ISA was culled from machine-readable XML files and stripped of the bloat. He built his version in 2022 with new CSS on top of it, and the addition of a quick search feature that, according to his comments on Hacker News, isn’t available in the official version.

“The aim has always been to make it the most comfortable and bullshit-free browsing experience for people who need these docs daily,” Palmisciano wrote in HN. Based on the responses the site seems to have plenty of fans.

That doesn’t matter to Arm, though: As far as the lawyers are concerned, Palmisciano’s site is a copyright violation due to its use of Arm trademarks and inclusion of copyrighted reference material for the Armv9-A and Armv9-A architecture.

Arm doesn’t care if Palmisciano’s project is well intentioned or for the benefit of the many software developers that write code for its chipsets, either: They want it offline by December 4 – 10 days from the publication of this story – or else.
As for what is going to happen, it seems like Jon’s Arm Reference will likely cease to exist in a little over a week – at least in its current form.

“Ideally I'd love to just get permission from Arm to keep the site up, but I'm pretty pessimistic about that,” Palmisciano told us. That said, Palmisciano has “already seen a few archives and mirrors already.” The HN thread discussing the takedown order includes links to several versions, and Palmisciano has another trick up his sleeve that he’s considering playing: Open-sourcing the software he used to build his ISA page.

“I'd also consider open-sourcing my tooling so that people can (for their own private use) turn the original XML downloads from Arm into an identical site they can host locally,” Palmisciano told us. He said that he'll likely tweet about opening the tooling if he does do so. He's also considered directing the URL for Jon's Arm reference to point to the open-source tool, but Arm wants the subdomain it's hosted on removed from his site as well, so that may not happen.
Arm has been in touch to defend itself as well, saying that Arm appreciates the efforts of people like Palmisciano, but that it still has to protect its brand, and documentation.

"We have a responsibility to ensure Arm is the primary source of technical resources and information and to protect the Arm brand," an Arm spokesperson told us. "Striking the right balance between third parties sharing helpful peer-to-peer resources while ensuring copyrighted Arm-related technical content is accurate has been critical to building the thriving ecosystem we have today."

In other words, if you’re an Arm dev worried about losing a valuable resource and having to turn to a website that bombards you with junk just to look up a few simple opcodes and operands you’d better find a backup host before next month.
That said, Arm is willing to work something out with Palmisciano, the company told us.

"We have recently flagged our concerns with regard to the use of Arm copyright content and the Arm brand on this website and shared the Arm trademark guidelines," Arm explained. "Our hope is to open a constructive dialogue, and we've asked that the website owner reach out as we seek to resolve this."

As Palmisciano posted on HN, Arm is asking for removal of its trademark and copyrighted documentation. That, Palmisciano said, "seems hard to work around while still keeping the site useful." He also followed up around 8.30 pm GMT on Tuesday to let us know that he has not yet heard directly from Arm. ®

80315362768f2ecf: A Romanian hacker, armed with only an open source coding agent, a Chrome browser, and a Mac, tried multiple ways to break into a financial services firm, ultimately found an access key - luckily, it was a decoy - and carried out an entire (almost) attack in under six minutes.

It’s a stark reminder that miscreants don’t need sophisticated malware - as in the Binance heist - or AI pen-testing tools like ARTEX to carry out intrusions into critical networks. Open source coding agents, and specifically OpenCode in this case, also work just fine.

“What surprised me most was how little it took and the toolkit: a free coding agent, the curl that comes with every Mac and an ordinary Chrome, all from one laptop,” Jesta co-founder and CTO Lior Finkelshtein told The Register. “Until now I thought that we had more time until tools like OpenCode are used in offensive operations. This incident shows us that it's already in use in the field, and we will probably see more of that in the future.”

Jesta is a Tel Aviv-based security startup that builds defensive tools to detect and stop autonomous AI attacks. In a report shared exclusively with The Register, Finkelshtein documented an attempted intrusion targeting a major financial services company that’s also a Jesta customer - the security shop declined to say which one.

Jesta’s investigation into the incident determined that someone in Bucharest downloaded a free AI coding agent called OpenCode and pointed it at the financial services customer on November 16 at 4:24:57 a.m. ET.
'Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking'

OpenCode is an open source coding agent that lets users connect to more than 200 model providers or local models, including Anthropic’s Claude models, OpenAI’s GPTs, Google’s Gemini, DeepSeek, and Z.ai’s GLM. Jesta doesn’t know which model the attacker used, as there was nothing in the traffic that named the model. OpenCode's web fetch tool, however, did name itself, so Jesta knows the attacker used this coding agent - not a scanner - to do the dirty work.

“Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking,” Finkelshtein said in a Tuesday report about the agent-led attack. But, he added, nothing in the coding agent “stops you from pointing it at someone else's website either. When you do, the agent goes through the site the same way it goes through code. It reads, tries something, reads the result and tries the next thing, for as long as you let it run.”
That’s what it did in this operation, which took less than six minutes and cost the human operator nothing.

The first call came from a Chrome browser on a Mac, requesting the front page of one of the financial firm’s systems. The site refused it, and six seconds later, the same IPv6 address in Bucharest, on an ordinary DIGI Romania business line, tried again. It used the same Chrome version, but said it was an Android Pixel 10 phone (it wasn’t) to see if the site would let a phone in (it didn’t).

After failing to gain access through the front page, the agent asked the system for its API definition, which was also refused. Five seconds later, it tried a different address - this one was a decoy set up by Jesta - and it answered the agent, providing the readable file defining how the API works.

The agent read the document, and 13 seconds later followed a link it contained. At 4:26:01 a.m. ET, Jesta’s defenses marked the website visitor as an AI agent, opened a case, and from here on out, everything the agent accessed was contained inside a fake environment designed to trick intruders. This included a phony key, which the attacker then used to attempt to break into the company’s systems.

“It worked like a developer,” Finkelshtein said about the coding agent. “It read the API docs and did what they said. It found a key and used it. It checked whether the lock was real, then made up a key of its own and tried that. None of the threat feeds the customer has knew the address, so a blocklist would never have stopped it. The bar for doing this is now installing an app. Think about how many people can do that.”
'No blocklist would have helped'

In addition to OpenCode, the attacker used only Chrome 157, both in desktop and mobile modes, and curl/8.7.1, a command-line tool that has shipped with every Mac since macOS 15. The agent passed information between the three tools. It included the planted key in a command-line request and then tested three scenarios – using the decoy key, no key, and a fabricated key – to determine whether what it found in the API documentation was legit.

It also tried multiple URLs using the browser. While it ultimately identified a valid endpoint, it attempted to read from one that accepts only data submissions, so its request was blocked again. Five minutes and 44 seconds after the first request, it gave up, and the logs haven’t detected any activity from this same intruder since then.
The security shop and its customer disclosed the activity to law enforcement and told us it’s “being handled.”
While the attacker wasn’t able to steal anything in this attempt, security teams still need to take note, according to Finkelshtein.

“No blocklist would have helped” detect the malicious traffic, he explained. “Most security tools still decide by asking whether an address is known to be bad, and for this one the answer was no. If that key had been real, it would have been in.”

Instead of blocklists, Finkelshtein suggests paying attention to what the visitor does. In this case, several of its actions gave it away - including following a link that only existed inside an API doc, using a desktop browser and a fake phone, then curl, all from the same address within minutes, and trying multiple keys - including one with a made up name and then no key - within seconds.

“Open source lets anyone build software without a big team,” Finkelshtein wrote in the Tuesday blog. “AI is doing the same for hacking. The skill is in the model, the model is a setting, and the person giving the instructions doesn't need to know how any of it works.” ®
